I love this game, 100% — but a lot of the time, love alone can't carry us through.

Sure, I've only put in a little over a thousand hours. For this game, I'm still just a beginner, and maybe it's too early to say I can't go on. But why can't we read the signs from a small sample? At least I started playing in early 2024 — back then, the game was nowhere near as frustrating as it is now. So for new players just picking it up today, what's going to keep them going? A bunch of irrelevant updates that don't even matter? (Updates that, even worse, make it, well, worse.)

Of course, the same old song — the god-awful anti-cheat — is the main reason I'm writing this review. But hey, I get it if you can't get anti-cheat right. After all, even those kernel-level anti-cheat games can't stop cheaters, so why should you be any different, right?

But trust has become a huge issue. I remember a while back, when an announcement said VAC had been updated, the community was buzzing with optimism. Everyone said aimbot scripts in deathmatch had dropped. So as soon as I had some free time, I jumped into a deathmatch game with high hopes. But nope — still plenty of script bots. True, maybe you did ban a wave of them, but new ones popped up just as fast. The deathmatch environment was better for, what, one morning at best?

You know why. The Armory Pass made it insanely fast for a prime account to turn a profit. Farming studios saw dollar signs, and you couldn't be bothered to care — they bought prime accounts and Armory Passes, you provided the servers. I remember back on October 3rd, our group chat was all hyped about the Armory Pass, everyone even bought one to try it out. Little did we know that script-farming bots would explode like never before after that.

You guys seem to have tried — slowing down XP gain. But that doesn't just affect bots; it hits us normal players too. We don't have much time to game anymore. Most of the time when we get together, it's under the excuse of weekly drops. But official matchmaking is an absolute circus. Wins and losses aren't even up to us — half the time we can't string together a few rounds, and we're all just exhausted. We end up logging off one by one, grinding some XP in deathmatch instead.

But deathmatch is f*cking infested with bots. Some of them I can't even tell apart anymore — now they even turn on their mics. Can you f*cking believe that? The first time I heard someone with an open mic, just gunshots and footsteps, no talking, I thought, "f*ck this as*hole, just here to annoy everyone." I even turned on my own mic to blast music. But later I realized — those guys with open mics? They were bots.

I'm furious, no question. These bots are practically indistinguishable from real players now. And they have wallhacks and aimbots, with settings ranging from subtle to blatant. So every time I get tilted by a bot, I teabag them, I type insults in chat. I know these digital entities don't feel a thing, but ♥♥♥♥ — some low-setting bots even lock onto dead bodies and teabag back. So ♥♥♥♥ it, I'll teabag anyway.

Just now there was this guy — I thought he was a bot, so I teabagged and flamed him. But turns out he wasn't, because he fired back. I don't think bots can do that yet. I know I started that fight, which makes me feel like an as*hole too.

Open the store page — almost all the most helpful reviews are negative, and they're all written earnestly. No way that's just review-bombing. It really makes me think — everyone says Valve cares about the community. So can Valve not see these negative reviews? Or do they just not give a f*ck?

Valve: "We value community feedback."
Lie detector: 👎👎👎

Lie detector: 👎👎👎

So f*ck it. F*ck you, Valve. Keep ruining this game.

7.500,00 horas jogadas deve significar algo para realizar uma análise, correto? Vamos lá!

- Sobre o jogo: aquele FPS que atende desde o jogador casual, até o jogador mais empenhado (nerd) que curte ficar bom de verdade e entender mais das mecânicas que o jogo oferece. No começo você vai demorar um bom tempo para aprender o básico do jogo, acredite, essa é a melhor fase, aproveite-a muito bem.
- Minha maior dica para esse jogo? Assim como qualquer um outro, jogue com amigos, priorize a diversão, lembre-se que para a maioria dos jogadores isso é um mero passa tempo, então seja inteligente e passe seu tempo da melhor maneira possível. Caso não tenha amigos que jogam, garanto que vai fazer muita amizade massa, nesses 10 anos de CSGO/CS2, tenho inúmeros amigos que o jogo me proporcionou.

- Gosta de saber o lado ruim/negativo de qualquer jogo, e quer saber qual é o desse aqui? 
Ok, você pediu: em um jogo com tanta tradição, que tem um reinado quase que imbatível competitivamente, você pode (e vai) chegar em um determinado momento, se frustar muito, e perguntar "como uma organização tão grande quanto a VALVE pode abrir tanto a mão de realmente querer acabar com os cheaters em seu próprio jogo?", você vai muitas vezes ver que chegou uma grande atualização, esperar que eles tenham atualizado seu anti-cheater e quando abrir o jogo: boooom, mais uma coleção de skins (ao que parece, acabar com cheater não dá dinheiro pra eles infelizmente). 
Caso já tenha escutado (minimamente) sobre o game, deve ter percebido o quanto a comunidade reclama disso (cheaters), e eu posso garantir que na maioria das vezes não é choro (eu sou um player antigo, nas plataformas competitivas sou level máximo em todas, não é qualquer player que eu vou achar que é cheater, mas no modo ranqueado desse jogo, está totalmente infestado, são jogadores que não disfarçam minimamente que estão usando alguma trapaça). 
Quer ter uma ideia? Hoje em dia jogo 99% das vezes em plataformas terceiras (que tenham um anti-cheater próprio) para ter uma garantia maior de que não vou cair contra cheaters (obviamente que no meu caso, também jogo nessas plataformas visando um nível de competitividade maior). Consegue mensurar o quão frustante para um player casual deve ser ter que: comprar seu jogo> descobrir uma plataforma que não é do próprio jogo> baixar o anti-cheater dela> abrir o jogo nessa plataforma> entender como ela funciona, tudo isso para EVITAR CAIR CONTRA CHEATERS, ou melhor, por incompetência da empresa por trás do jogo.

- Conclusão: fora esse ônus (que é bem irritante) dos cheaters, garanto que o bônus compensa bastante toda a experiência, o dia que a desenvolvedora realmente se importar em acabar com os cheaters de verdade, esse jogo não terá mais reclamações.

CS2 hat gutes Gunplay, aber Trust Factor und Ranked sind ein verdammter Witz

CS2 könnte ein richtig guter Shooter sein. Das Gunplay macht Spaß und grundsätzlich spiele ich das Spiel gerne. Aber alles rund um Trust Factor, Matchmaking und Anti Cheat fühlt sich wie eine einzige beschissene Verarsche an.

Ich habe mittlerweile über 1.000 Stunden und mehr als 500 Matches gespielt. Letzte Season hatte ich einen grünen Trust Factor. Mein Kollege hatte dagegen einen roten. Dann hat er sich Skins über eine Drittanbieter Seite gekauft. Plötzlich hatte er einen grünen Trust Factor und ich einen roten. Nachdem er die Skins wieder verkauft hatte, war meiner wieder grün und seiner wieder rot.

Natürlich kann ich nicht beweisen, wie Valve den Trust Factor genau berechnet, weil dieses undurchsichtige Scheißsystem absichtlich niemandem erklärt wird. Aber genau das ist das Problem. Niemand weiß, was wirklich zählt. Streamer und Influencer erzählen, man müsse Geld auf Steam einzahlen oder Skins kaufen, um seinen Trust Factor zu verbessern. Andere behaupten, Käufe bei Drittanbietern würden überhaupt keinen Unterschied machen. Trotzdem passieren solche auffälligen Wechsel. Was soll man von diesem Müll bitte halten?

Der Trust Factor wirkt nicht wie ein seriöses Sicherheitssystem, sondern wie ein manipuliertes Glücksspiel, bei dem niemand die Regeln kennt. Heute spielst du in normalen Lobbys und morgen landest du ohne erkennbaren Grund mit verdächtigen Accounts, Smurfs, Bots und Cheatern zusammen. Transparenz gibt es keine. Eine vernünftige Erklärung von Valve gibt es natürlich auch nicht.

Das Ranked System ist genauso lächerlich. Die Ränge fühlen sich teilweise komplett zufällig an, die Matchqualität schwankt extrem und faire Spiele sind offenbar reine Glückssache. Dazu kommt ein Anti Cheat, das gefühlt nur existiert, damit Valve behaupten kann, dass CS2 überhaupt eines besitzt.

Valve verdient mit Steam, Cases, Skins und Gebühren Milliarden, bekommt es aber trotzdem nicht auf die Reihe, ein vernünftiges Anti Cheat System bereitzustellen. Wie kann es sein, dass eine externe Plattform wie FACEIT weniger Cheater und ein besseres Anti Cheat besitzt als der eigentliche Entwickler des Spiels?

Valve könnte problemlos einen eigenen sicheren Launcher entwickeln oder endlich richtig Geld in ein funktionierendes Anti Cheat investieren. Stattdessen werden weiterhin Cases verkauft, während sich die Spieler durch verseuchte Lobbys quälen dürfen. Hauptsache Valve verdient weiter Geld. Der Zustand des Spiels scheint dabei vollkommen scheißegal zu sein.

Selbst Deathmatch ist inzwischen kaum noch spielbar, weil ständig irgendwelche Accounts automatisiert hochgelevelt oder gebottet werden. Man betritt einen Server und sieht teilweise mehr Bots und Farm Accounts als normale Spieler. Das ist einfach nur peinlich und zeigt, wie wenig Valve sein eigenes Spiel unter Kontrolle hat.

CS2 hat eine starke Grundlage, aber Valve behandelt das Spiel wie einen verdammten Geldautomaten. Hauptsache Skins, Cases und Gebühren bringen weiter Kohle. Ob das Matchmaking fair ist, der Trust Factor nachvollziehbar funktioniert oder die Server voller Cheater und Bots sind, interessiert offenbar keine Sau.

Guter Shooter, aber ein katastrophales System dahinter. Trust Factor und Ranked sind undurchsichtige Scheiße, das Anti Cheat ist eine Lachnummer und Valve melkt die Community weiter, während das eigentliche Spiel immer mehr verrottet.

CS2 has great gunplay, but Trust Factor and Ranked are a complete joke

CS2 could be a genuinely great shooter. The gunplay is enjoyable and at its core I actually like the game. Unfortunately, everything surrounding Trust Factor, matchmaking and Anti Cheat feels like one massive pile of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

I have played for more than 1,000 hours and over 500 matches. Last season I had a green Trust Factor while my friend had a red one. He then bought skins from a third party marketplace. Suddenly his Trust Factor appeared green while mine became red. After he sold the skins again, mine appeared green and his went back to red.

Obviously, I cannot prove exactly how Valve calculates Trust Factor because this shady and deliberately vague system is never properly explained. That is exactly the problem. Nobody knows what actually affects it. Streamers and influencers claim that depositing money on Steam or buying skins improves your Trust Factor. Other people claim that buying skins from third party websites makes absolutely no difference. Yet suspicious changes like this still happen. What the hell are players supposed to believe?

Trust Factor does not feel like a serious security system. It feels like a manipulated lottery where nobody knows the rules. One day you get normal matches and the next day you are thrown into lobbies full of suspicious accounts, smurfs, bots and cheaters for no obvious reason. There is no transparency and of course Valve does not provide a proper explanation either.

The ranking system is just as pathetic. Ranks often feel completely random, match quality is wildly inconsistent and getting a fair game seems to depend entirely on luck. Then there is the Anti Cheat, which sometimes feels like it only exists so Valve can claim that CS2 technically has one.

Valve makes billions from Steam, cases, skins and marketplace fees, yet somehow cannot provide a competent Anti Cheat system. How the hell does an external platform like FACEIT manage to offer better Anti Cheat and fewer cheaters than the actual developer of the game?

Valve could easily develop its own secure launcher or finally invest serious money into a working Anti Cheat solution. Instead, it keeps selling cases while players are forced to suffer through contaminated matchmaking. As long as Valve keeps making money, the actual condition of the game apparently does not matter.

Even Deathmatch is becoming unplayable because so many accounts are being botted or automatically levelled. You join a server and sometimes see more farming accounts and bots than actual players. It is embarrassing and shows how little control Valve has over its own game.

CS2 has a strong foundation, but Valve treats the game like a damn ATM. As long as skins, cases and fees keep printing money, it apparently does not matter whether matchmaking is fair, Trust Factor makes any sense or the servers are full of cheaters and bots.

Good shooter, absolutely terrible systems behind it. Trust Factor and Ranked are opaque garbage, the Anti Cheat is a joke and Valve keeps milking the community while the actual game slowly rots.

DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME - CHEATERS SIMULATOR 2
 At this point, CS2 feels less like a competitive FPS and more like a cheater showcase.
 Every time you try to play seriously, you run into someone blatantly wallhacking, aimbotting, or using some other ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cheat. And the worst part ? The anti-cheat feels completly useless.
 How is a game this popular still struggling with such a massive cheating problem ? You can report someone, move on, and then meet another obvious cheater in the next match. There is barely any confidence that reports actually lead to anything.
 0/10 anti-cheat. 0/10 trust in matchmaking.

Do not come back to Counter-Strike. Seriously.

It genuinely hurts to see what has happened to a game that so many of us have loved since childhood.

Counter-Strike used to be about competitive gameplay, skill, teamwork and the satisfaction of getting better. Today, it increasingly feels like the game is being left to rot while the focus is on skins, gambling-adjacent mechanics and finding yet another way to squeeze the last few cents out of the player base.

And the cheating situation is absolutely ridiculous.

Serious competitive gameplay simply does not exist anymore when you constantly have to wonder whether the person killing you is actually playing the game or running some kind of cheat. The fact that a game of this size still has such a laughable anti-cheat situation is beyond disappointing.

Apparently, fixing the actual game isn't quite as profitable as selling another skin.

What makes it even worse is that this isn't some random game nobody cares about. This is Counter-Strike. A game that shaped an entire generation of PC gamers and that many of us have been playing and loving for decades.

Seeing the developers seemingly ignore the problems that actually matter while continuing to monetize the game is honestly just sad.

So if you're thinking about getting back into CS after a few years away: don't.

Save yourself the frustration, the cheaters and the realization that the game you remember isn't really there anymore.

[h1]CS2, czyli do zobaczenia jutro, chociaż nigdy więcej[/h1]

Counter Strike 2 to wyjątkowe doświadczenie społeczne. Gra, w której wszyscy narzekają na cheaterów, wszyscy mają dość i wszyscy są przekonani, że kiedyś było lepiej. Po czym ktoś na Discordzie pyta „to co, piątego szukamy?” i nagle cała grupa poszkodowanych jest gotowa na kolejne dwie godziny.

[b]Nikt nie poleca. Każdy gra. Każdy zna kogoś, kto skończył z CS-em.[/b]
[i]Ten ktoś właśnie wysłał zaproszenie do lobby.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Antycheat, czyli ochrona na poziomie naklejki „obiekt monitorowany”[/h2]

Mam wrażenie, że VAC działa jak światło w lodówce. Niby jest, ale trudno stwierdzić, co robi, kiedy nikt nie patrzy.

Przeciwnik śledzi cię przez ścianę, celuje w głowę jeszcze przed twoim narodzeniem i wychyla dokładnie wtedy, kiedy wyciągasz granat. System patrzy na to z niewzruszonym spokojem urzędnika, któremu za trzy minuty kończy się zmiana.

[b]Werdykt?[/b] Pewnie dobry fotel gamingowy.

Oczywiście nie każdy lepszy gracz oszukuje. Czasem ktoś ma świetny refleks, zna mapę i potrafi strzelać. Potrafię to uszanować. Trochę trudniej uszanować człowieka, który zdobywa informacje o mojej pozycji szybciej niż ja.

[u]Antycheat powinien wzbudzać strach u oszustów. Obecnie wzbudza głównie nadzieję u reszty.[/u]

[strike]Spokojnie, następna aktualizacja na pewno rozwiąże problem.[/strike]
Spokojnie, następna aktualizacja przynajmniej da nam kolejny powód, żeby sprawdzić.

[h3]Najpopularniejsze wyjaśnienia podejrzanych zagrań[/h3]

[list]
[*]Usłyszał cię. Stałeś nieruchomo, ale podobno głośno myślisz.
[*]Ma dobre słuchawki. Najwyraźniej odbierają również obraz.
[*]To smurf. Na głównym koncie prawdopodobnie zarządza ruchem satelitów.
[*]Zna wszystkie kąty. Szczególnie ten, pod którym siedzisz przed monitorem.
[*]Miał info. Jeszcze nie ustalono, z którego ministerstwa.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]A potem trafia się ten jeden normalny mecz[/h2]

I nagle wszystko zaczyna mieć sens.

Strzelanie daje ogromną satysfakcję. Czysty headshot z AK potrafi poprawić humor skuteczniej niż cały dzień odpoczynku. Dobrze rzucony smoke, udane wejście na bombsite i odbicie rundy, którą już zdążyliście przegrać w głowach, sprawiają, że siedzisz bliżej monitora, choć przed chwilą miałeś kończyć.

Zostajesz sam na trzech. Koledzy po raz pierwszy tego wieczoru milkną. Jeden przeciwnik pada, drugi też, trzeciego łapiesz na przeładowaniu. Rozbrajasz bombę, na Discordzie wybucha radość i przez chwilę jesteś człowiekiem, o którym powinno się robić dokumenty.

[b]W następnej rundzie oślepiasz czterech kolegów i giniesz z własnym granatem w ręce.[/b]

Równowaga we wszechświecie zostaje przywrócona.

To właśnie jest największa siła CS2. Możesz znać mapę na pamięć, a kolejny mecz i tak przyniesie coś nowego. Raz wygrywasz dzięki celności, raz dzięki pomysłowi, a raz dlatego, że przeciwnik popełnił jeszcze głupszy błąd od ciebie.

[i]Ten ostatni rodzaj zwycięstwa jest mi szczególnie bliski.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Gra zespołowa, czyli pięć osób i sześć różnych planów[/h2]

Z dobrą ekipą CS2 jest kapitalny. Wspólne akcje, szybkie informacje, wzajemne ratowanie sytuacji i śmiech po rundzie, której przebiegu nie da się logicznie wyjaśnić.

Z losowymi graczami otrzymujesz dodatkowo bezpłatny kurs cierpliwości i podstawy komunikacji międzynarodowej w warunkach kryzysowych.

Jeden mówi „gramy spokojnie”, po czym ginie po ośmiu sekundach. Drugi oszczędza broń tak długo, że można podejrzewać więź emocjonalną. Trzeci ma mikrofon uruchamiany wyłącznie po własnej śmierci. Czwarty niesie bombę w miejsce, którego nie obejmowała nawet wycieczka szkolna po mapie.

Piąty to ja. Oczywiście bez winy. Jak każdy autor recenzji.

[u]Największym cudem tej gry nie jest wygrany clutch. Jest nim pięć osób, które jednocześnie rozumieją „nie wychylaj”.[/u]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Standardowy wieczór z CS2[/h2]

[olist]
[*]Odpalasz grę z nastawieniem, że dzisiaj tylko dwa spokojne mecze.
[*]Pierwszy traktujesz jako rozgrzewkę, więc porażka się nie liczy.
[*]Drugi przegrywasz, ale przecież nie można kończyć na porażce.
[*]Trzeci wygrywasz, więc szkoda marnować dobrą passę.
[*]Czwarty przegrywasz, bo ktoś powiedział „ostatni”.
[*]Ogłaszasz zakończenie kariery.
[*]Sprawdzasz, kto jeszcze siedzi na Discordzie.
[*]Klikasz „Graj”.
[/olist]

[spoiler]Rano nie jesteś wypoczęty, ale za to masz mniej punktów.[/spoiler]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Ekonomia też zasługuje na wyróżnienie[/h2]

Gra uczy odpowiedzialnego zarządzania pieniędzmi. Dowiadujesz się, kiedy oszczędzać, kiedy inwestować i dlaczego kolega kupił AWP bez kamizelki, mimo że wszyscy ustalili eco.

Po kilku rundach zaczynasz rozumieć budżet drużyny lepiej niż własne wydatki. Wiesz, komu rzucić broń, ile zostawić na granaty i kiedy zakup karabinu będzie błędem.

Potem oglądasz skina i uznajesz, że wirtualny magazynek jednak powinien być fioletowy.

[b]Wiedza finansowa została zdobyta. Zastosowanie odłożono na później.[/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Ostateczny werdykt[/h2]

CS2 potrafi zmęczyć, zirytować i wystawić cierpliwość na próbę. Antycheat zdecydowanie potrzebuje czegoś więcej niż naszej wiary, a podejrzane mecze skutecznie odbierają przyjemność z rywalizacji.

Ale pod tym wszystkim nadal jest [b]świetna strzelanka[/b]. Wymagająca, emocjonująca i niesamowicie satysfakcjonująca, kiedy wszystko zagra. Celność ma znaczenie, współpraca ma znaczenie, a jedna dobra decyzja potrafi odwrócić całą rundę. Z kumplami można tu spędzić mnóstwo naprawdę udanych wieczorów.

To gra, o której najwięcej złego mówią ludzie, którzy nie mają czasu na inne gry, bo właśnie grają w CS2.

I genuinely cannot recommend CS2 in its current state.

The core game is still good. The gunplay is great, the movement feels satisfying, the maps are iconic, and Counter-Strike is still one of the best competitive FPS concepts ever made.

But none of that matters when the competitive experience is completely destroyed by cheaters.

Premier, Competitive, and even other modes constantly have players that are suspicious as hell. You see people tracking through walls, pre-firing positions they should have no information about, perfectly reading rotations, staring at players through objects, and doing things that make absolutely no sense from a normal player's perspective.

And the worst part is that Valve seems like they simply do not give a ♥♥♥♥.

The anti-cheat feels completely useless far too often.

Players can report obvious cheaters again and again, yet you still see suspicious accounts playing for weeks or months. Some of them have high ranks, expensive inventories, old accounts, badges, and plenty of playtime, which makes the whole situation even more frustrating.

At this point, every good player becomes suspicious because Valve has allowed the cheating problem to destroy the trust between players.

That is one of the biggest problems.

Counter-Strike is supposed to be about skill, game sense, aim, utility, communication, positioning, and teamwork.

But when you die and your first thought is not:

"That guy played better than me."

and instead it is:

"Was that guy wallhacking?"

then your competitive game has a serious problem.

Even if someone is completely legit, the current environment makes you doubt everything.

That alone ruins the experience.

Valve keeps adding cases, skins, cosmetics, events, updates, and other content, but where is the serious anti-cheat improvement?

Where is the system that actually makes cheaters scared of losing their accounts?

Where is the fast reaction to obvious cheating?

Where is the transparency?

Where is the feeling that Valve is actually fighting for the competitive integrity of their own game?

Because right now, from the player's perspective, it often feels like Valve cares more about keeping the economy and skin market alive than protecting the actual competitive experience.

A competitive FPS cannot survive on skins alone.

You can have beautiful skins, expensive knives, new cases, new maps, and fancy updates, but if players don't trust the matchmaking system, the entire competitive foundation starts falling apart.

And honestly, the cheating problem is not some small issue anymore.

It is one of the main things people talk about when discussing CS2.

When legitimate players stop enjoying the game because they constantly feel like they are playing against wallhackers or other cheaters, something has gone seriously wrong.

And no, telling players to "just play FACEIT" is not an excuse.

Valve owns Counter-Strike.

Valve runs Premier.

Valve runs Competitive.

Valve makes money from the game.

The official matchmaking experience should not require a third-party platform just to have a better chance of playing fair matches.

Players should be able to launch CS2, queue Premier, and trust that they are playing against legitimate opponents.

That should be the absolute minimum expectation.

Instead, we have reached a point where losing a match sometimes feels less frustrating than not knowing whether the match was even legitimate in the first place.

That is terrible for any competitive game.

Valve needs to stop treating cheating like a secondary problem.

Anti-cheat should be one of the highest priorities in CS2.

Not cases.

Not cosmetic updates.

Not another skin collection.

Not another small UI change.

ANTI-CHEAT.

Competitive integrity.

Actual bans.

Faster detection.

Better systems.

Real consequences for cheating.

Because right now it feels like Valve doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about the anti-cheat situation or the players whose matches are being ruined by cheaters.

CS2 has the potential to be an incredible competitive game.

But potential means nothing if the matchmaking experience is full of distrust, frustration, and suspicious players.

I love Counter-Strike.

That is exactly why this situation is so disappointing.

I don't want CS2 to fail.

I want Valve to actually protect the game.

Until the cheating problem is taken seriously and the official matchmaking experience becomes trustworthy again, I cannot recommend CS2.

Fix the anti-cheat.

Fix Premier.

Start protecting legitimate players.

The community deserves better.

Игра после обновления вылетает как девятиклассница из окна пятнадцатого этажа после неразделенной любви. Разрабы криворукие.

На релизе игра казалась чем-то невероятным — пусть и сырым, как мне тогда казалось.

Люди играли исключительно по фану: устраивали безумные зарубы, экспериментировали, веселились и создавали те самые моменты, ради которых в королевские битвы вообще хотелось играть. Лишь единицы тогда сидели по кустам и углам, выдрачивая каждый пиксель и превращая матч в соревнование по терпению.

Прошло почти десять лет, и самое забавное — игра до сих пор ощущается как сырая недоделка. Только теперь это уже не «сырой, но невероятно перспективный проект», а попросту скучная и морально устаревшая королевская битва.

При этом нельзя отрицать её влияние на жанр. На момент выхода она была событием и подарила массу эмоций. Но время оказалось к ней беспощадно.

Вклад в жанр королевских битв — 10/10.

PUBG je jedna z her, u kterých je těžké mluvit o jejich významu, aniž bychom zmínili celý žánr battle royale. Právě PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds totiž patří mezi tituly, které tenhle princip dostaly do mainstreamu a ukázaly milionům hráčů, jak zábavné může být začít zápas prakticky s ničím, postupně hledat vybavení a snažit se zůstat posledním přeživším.

A i když dnes existuje obrovské množství battle royale her, PUBG má pořád svoje místo. Není tak barevné jako Fortnite, nesnaží se být přehnaně arkádové a jeho kouzlo stojí především na napětí, které vzniká z jednoduchého faktu, že další souboj může během několika sekund ukončit celý váš zápas.

Právě to mě na PUBG vždycky bavilo. Začátek hry může působit relativně klidně. Seskočíte, hledáte zbraně, vybavení a snažíte se dostat do bezpečné zóny. Jenže s postupujícím časem se prostor zmenšuje a počet hráčů klesá. Najednou už každý zvuk znamená potenciální problém. Výstřel někde v dálce vás donutí přemýšlet, jestli pokračovat, nebo změnit trasu. Auto projíždějící kolem může znamenat, že se někdo blíží. A když se dostanete mezi posledních několik hráčů, atmosféra se úplně změní.

PUBG navíc dokáže vytvořit situace, které si člověk pamatuje mnohem déle než běžné multiplayerové zápasy. Někdy vyhrajete díky perfektně provedenému útoku, jindy přežijete jen proto, že si vás protivník nevšiml. Občas se všechno pokazí během několika sekund a celý zápas, do kterého jste investovali třeba dvacet minut, skončí jednou špatnou střelou.

Přesto mám u PUBG jeden problém, který je pro mě osobně poměrně zásadní. A tím je konec PUBG Lite. Tahle verze pro mě nebyla jen nějakou osekanou variantou plnohodnotného PUBG. Měla jednu obrovskou výhodu: byla výrazně dostupnější pro hráče s horším hardwarem. Díky tomu jsem si mohl zahrát PUBG i s kamarády, kteří neměli počítače schopné rozjet klasickou verzi. A tenkrát jsem ani já neměl žádnou mašinu, nicméně moje tehdejší Gtx 1050 rozjela lite verzi s přehledem. A právě multiplayer je přitom podle mě jedním z hlavních důvodů, proč podobné hry vůbec hrát. Nejde jen o samotné vítězství. Jde o to, že s několika kamarády skočíte na mapu, začnete si rozdávat vybavení, plánujete další postup a během několika minut se z původně jednoduchého zápasu může stát úplný chaos.

Zrušení Lite verze proto vnímám jako škodu. Ne každý má herní počítač, který zvládne moderní multiplayerové hry bez problémů. PUBG Lite dokázalo tenhle problém elegantně obejít a otevřít hru i lidem, kteří by si jinak PUBG zahrát nemohli. Dnes už se tak může stát, že mám chuť si PUBG zahrát s partou, ale někteří kamarádi se jednoduše nepřipojí, protože jejich počítač plnou verzi neutáhne. A to je možná trochu ironické. Hra, která kdysi dokázala přivést battle royale k obrovskému množství hráčů, je dnes pro část lidí hůře dostupná než dříve.

Samotnému PUBG ale nemám příliš co zásadního vytknout. Není to hra, která by mě pokaždé dokázala nadchnout, a po letech už samozřejmě nepůsobí tak revolučně jako v době, kdy battle royale teprve získávalo svůj dnešní význam. Jenže to není úplně její chyba. Když jste jedním z titulů, které pomohly vytvořit celý žánr, je těžké být pořád tím překvapivým nováčkem. PUBG je dnes především osvědčený základ. Fungující střelba, velké mapy, napětí, loot, taktika a především nepředvídatelnost. Každý zápas může vypadat úplně jinak a nikdy nemáte jistotu, jak skončí.

A přestože už PUBG dávno není jediným battle royale na trhu, jeho historický význam mu nikdo nevezme. Je to jedna z her, které pomohly změnit multiplayer a udělat z battle royale jeden z největších fenoménů moderního hraní. Za mě je tedy PUBG pořád fajn hra. Ne bezchybná, ne revoluční jako kdysi, ale stále dostatečně zábavná na to, abych se k ní dokázal vrátit. Mrzí mě jen, že už u ní nemůžu mít všechny kamarády, se kterými jsem ji hrával dřív. A pak vám nezbývá než doufat, že někdo znovu otevře dveře i těm počítačům, které už dnes nestíhají držet krok.

[h1]A game that never reached it's true potential.[/h1]

This is easily one of the best games made in the past 10 years, with that said... 

Through poor management, cheating issues, poor optimization, scope creep, it failed in making a lasting impact in the gaming community. Yes, there is still an active community but there was a time where if this game had the attention it deserved it could have had the same legacy that counter-strike had with FPS competitive shooters, that's how good the concept was.

Somewhere in 2019-2020 there seemed to be a shift to prioritize micro transactions and the skin market, which basically turned the game into a cheap version of itself that felt more like an arcade shooter. Bunny ears and all. 

Then they launched the mobile version which sucked the soul out the game. More skins, micro transactions, simplistic gaming mechanics. The PC version started to feel more like the mobile version eventually.

New maps, game modes, weapons, etc... were delayed for way too long. Performance still felt sluggish even with multiple rounds of updates, it just never got that polished AAA feel until 3-4 years into release. 

There was a massive exodus of players who felt like the project had been abandoned and the game started feeling stale and dated. The competitive scene in this game was very fun to participate in, but in classic PUBG/KRAFTON fashion, they decided to prioritize third-person competitive play over FPS which alienated everyone except Asia regions.

PUBG was a fantastic game that has been plagued by poor decisions since launch. 

For those people that had been there since beta, it's a total heart break of what this game once was and what could have been.

Coming from a guy who has over 1300+ of PLAYED hours.

[h1]Attrapez-les tous ! Et faites-les travailler ![/h1]

[i]Palworld mélange plusieurs styles, où l'amitié avec les créatures passe visiblement par leur faire fabriquer des armes et trimer à l’usine. [/i]

À savoir avant tout : je suis un joueur solo. Je n'ai absolument pas testé le multi, mais j'imagine que ça doit être tout aussi fun à plusieurs. En tout cas, même seul, il y a de quoi faire pour ne pas s'ennuyer.

Le concept est assez simple : prenez un jeu de survie en monde ouvert, ajoutez-y des créatures à capturer, à entraîner et à faire combattre, saupoudrez le tout d'un peu de construction, de craft et d'armes à feu… et vous obtenez [b]Palworld[/b]. 

On commence sur une île, avec rien dans les poches, puis on construit progressivement sa petite base. Il faut explorer, récolter des ressources, fabriquer son équipement et améliorer ses installations. Jusque-là, rien de particulièrement nouveau pour un jeu de survie.

Puis arrivent les Pals.
Ces petites créatures peuplent le monde et peuvent être capturées pour combattre à nos côtés, nous aider dans notre base ou encore être utilisées pour produire différentes ressources. Chacun possède ses propres compétences et affinités, ce qui pousse rapidement à constituer une équipe adaptée à nos besoins.

Et c'est là que ça devient particulièrement addictif.

On part explorer pour trouver de nouveaux Pals, on les capture, on teste leurs capacités, on les fait travailler dans notre base, puis on repart à la recherche de nouvelles créatures encore plus intéressantes. On se retrouve rapidement à vouloir tous les collectionner…
Sauf qu'ici, quand votre Pal ne vous sert plus à rien, vous pouvez toujours lui trouver une utilité dans une chaîne de production à le faire travailler jusqu’à épuisement.

Parce que oui, [b]Palworld[/b] n'est pas vraiment le monde merveilleux des monstres de poche. C'est plutôt Pokémon si la Team Rocket avait gagné et décidé de pousser le vice de l’esclavagisme à fond.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3778546021 

Et pourtant, c'est probablement ce qui rend le jeu aussi amusant.
L'exploration est agréable, le monde est suffisamment vaste pour donner envie d'aller voir ce qu'il y a derrière la prochaine colline, et les combats sont suffisamment dynamiques pour éviter de tomber dans le simple copier-coller du système au tour par tour (là, y’a de l’action ! CA PETE !!!!).

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3765154271 

La construction et la gestion de la base apportent également une bonne dose de progression. On débloque de nouvelles technologies, de nouveaux bâtiments et de nouveaux équipements, ce qui permet progressivement de transformer notre petit campement précaire en véritable usine à ressources.

À cela, il faut également ajouter une histoire, des quêtes et tout ce qui a trait aux RPG. 
Car ce côté-là n'a pas non plus été oublié. L’île n’est pas déserte, différentes factions s’affrontent et différents objectifs vous attendent au fur et à mesure de votre progression.

Bon, le jeu n'est évidemment pas parfait. Certaines mécaniques peuvent manquer de finition, l'IA fait parfois des choses assez… créatives, et quelques aspects du système de survie ou de construction peuvent se montrer frustrants. Mais rien qui ne m'ait empêché de prendre énormément de plaisir à parcourir le monde et à remplir mon Palpedia (Paldex aurait été un peu trop proche, hein ?).

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3769649121 

Parce qu'au final, [b]Palworld[/b] est probablement ce qui se rapproche le plus du jeu idéal que j'aurais aimé voir paraître dans cette célèbre licence nipponne…
Un monde ouvert à explorer, presque 300 Pals à découvrir, de l'élevage, des combats, des quêtes et surtout une vraie sensation de liberté.

Et franchement, je ne suis pas certain de vouloir revenir en arrière.

Consider my creature collecting and base building itches scratched for a good while.

There's a LOT here that I enjoyed. The exploration was great, there's a wide variety of critters to catch, plenty of craftables to make, and the breeding mechanics can get crazy in-depth if you want to dig into them. In all honesty, I enjoyed this way more than I have the last few mainline Pokemon games I played. Will I 100% it? Probably not, but that's more just not wanting to bother tracking down all of the stat boosting relics than anything else.

There's a bit of jank to the combat in that certain beam type moves seem to melt anything regardless of typing, and the grind for resources can be pretty rough, but it's nothing insurmountable. It's clearly designed for multiplayer servers ala ARK, too. There's pretty obvious clearings for base building dotted around the map, and it feels a bit lonesome with no other activity in them.

Still, if you can get past the meme of "Pokemon with Guns", it's a good time.

✔ Удачное сочетание жанров. Palworld умудряется смешать в себе сразу несколько игр: немного Minecraft, ARK: Survival Evolved и Terraria. От каждой она берёт интересные идеи и собирает из них довольно необычную смесь.

✔ Огромное количество контента. Исследование мира, строительство базы, прокачка, ловля палов, сражения, производство и куча других занятий. Плюсов настолько много, что я просто заебусь их все перечислять)

✔ Палы. Система ловли и использования палов отлично вписывается в выживание. Они не просто коллекционные существа — их можно использовать в бою, на базе и для различных задач.

✔ Исследование мира. Мир достаточно большой, и исследовать его действительно интересно. Постоянно находишь новые места, ресурсы, палов и различные активности.

✔ Базы и автоматизация. Постепенно можно превратить свою базу в настоящую фабрику, где палы будут выполнять большую часть работы. За этим довольно интересно наблюдать и постоянно хочется что-то улучшать.

❌ Минусы:

❌ Просадки FPS на больших базах. Под конец игры, когда на базе становится слишком много палов, производительность может проседать примерно до 30 FPS на эпических настройках. Тут либо смириться, либо снижать графику.

❌ Музыка и звуки. Они просто нормальные. Не могу сказать, что они плохие, но и хорошими их назвать не получится. За всё прохождение я практически ничего из саундтрека даже не запомнил.

❌ Проценты ловли палов. У меня иногда складывалось ощущение, что эти проценты работают просто рандомно. Могу спокойно поймать пала с шансом 5–10%, а потом потратить кучу попыток на того, у кого шанс 75%+.

❌ Древние технологии. В конце игры у меня накопилось огромное количество очков древних технологий, при этом обычных постоянно не хватало. Было бы намного удобнее сделать какой-нибудь обменник или машину, которая могла бы конвертировать один тип очков в другой.

💬 Итог:

Palworld — игра, которая реально смогла меня затянуть. Почти 80 часов, весь основной сюжет и большая часть дополнительного контента — и при этом я всё равно получил огромное удовольствие.

Да, у игры есть проблемы с производительностью, звуком, системой процентов ловли и балансом технологических очков. Но самое интересное, что даже после того, как я перечислил столько недостатков, впечатление от игры у меня осталось очень положительное.

Если вы любите песочницы и выживачи — Palworld однозначно стоит попробовать.

Palworld’ü ilk yayınlandığı ve erken erişim sürecinde olduğu dönemlerde oynayanlardan biriyim. Hatta o zamanlar oyunu oynarken “Bunun her şeyi hatalı gibi” diyerek eleştirdiğimi çok net hatırlıyorum. Mekanikler, sistemler ve genel oynanış açısından birçok şeyin henüz oturmadığını düşünüyordum.

Fakat 1.0 sürümünün yayınlanmasının ardından oyuna tekrar bir şans vermeye karar verdim. Açıkçası karşılaştığım şey beklediğimden oldukça farklıydı. Stüdyonun oyunu ciddi anlamda elden geçirdiğini, eksiklerini büyük ölçüde toparladığını ve erken erişimdeki haline kıyasla çok daha oturmuş bir deneyim sunduğunu görmek beni gerçekten şaşırttı.

Hatta öyle ki, tekrar başladığım bu süreçte yaklaşık bir ay içerisinde 300 küsur saat oynadığımı fark ettim.

Palworld’ün en çok eleştirilen ve aynı zamanda en çok konuşulan taraflarından biri, başka oyunlardan fazlasıyla tanıdık gelen objeler, mekanikler ve fikirler barındırması. Bunu inkâr etmek zaten mümkün değil. Ancak bana göre Palworld’ü ilginç yapan şey tam olarak burada başlıyor.

Çünkü stüdyo, oyuncuların alıştığı klasik oyun mantığının dışına çıkarak birbirinden farklı türleri tek bir potada eritmiş. Hayatta kalma, açık dünya, üs kurma, üretim, keşif, savaş, yaratık toplama ve RPG mekaniklerini bir araya getirerek, ilk bakışta oldukça karmaşık görünen ancak parçaları birbirine şaşırtıcı derecede iyi uyum sağlayan bir yapı ortaya çıkarmış.

Başka oyunlarda gördüğümüz birçok mekanik Palworld içerisinde kendisine yer buluyor. Fakat önemli olan yalnızca bu mekaniklerin nereden geldiği değil, bunların bir araya getirildiğinde nasıl bir deneyim oluşturduğu. Palworld burada farklı türleri başarılı bir şekilde harmanlayarak, ortaya farklı türlerin başarılı bir sentezini çıkarmış.

Bu sentezin en büyük başarısı ise sistemlerin birbirinden bağımsız hissettirmemesi. Üs kurmanız Pallerle olan ilişkinizi, Pallerinizin yetenekleri üretim sisteminizi, keşif yaptığınız dünya ise savaş ve ilerleme sisteminizi doğrudan etkiliyor. Böylece oyundaki farklı mekanikler birbirini besleyen bir döngü oluşturuyor.

Ancak Palworld’ü yalnızca oynanış mekanikleri üzerinden değerlendirmek bence oyunun asıl ilginç tarafını gözden kaçırmak oluyor.

Oyunun biraz daha derinlerine indiğinizde, yanınızda dolaşan Pallerin aslında oyuncuya anlatmaya çalıştığı başka hikâyeler olduğunu fark ediyorsunuz. Bu anlatım doğrudan yüzünüze vurulmuyor; daha çok Pallerin karakterleri, davranışları ve dünyayla olan ilişkileri üzerinden kendisini gösteriyor.

Örneğin kıskançlık, tembellik ve öfke gibi insanlara özgü zaafların Pallerin karakterlerine ve davranışlarına yansıtılması oldukça dikkat çekici. Bunun yanında açlık, stres, yorgunluk, hastalık ve çeşitli sağlık sorunları gibi durumların da Pallerin davranışlarını ve çalışma düzenlerini doğrudan etkileyebilmesi, onları yalnızca oyunda kullanılan birer araç olmaktan çıkarıyor. Daha da ilginç olanı ise bu özelliklerin yalnızca tek tek Paller üzerinden değil, birbirleriyle ve oyuncuyla olan ilişkileri üzerinden de ortaya çıkması. Onlara nasıl davrandığınız, ne kadar çalıştırdığınız, ihtiyaçlarını ne kadar karşıladığınız ve onları nasıl yönlendirdiğiniz, zaman içerisinde Pallerin durumlarını ve davranışlarını değiştirebiliyor. Bu yönüyle oyun, oyuncuya yalnızca “sahip olduğun Pallerden ne kadar verim alabilirsin?” sorusunu değil, aynı zamanda “onlara nasıl davranıyorsun ve bunun sonucunda neye dönüşüyorlar?” sorusunu da sorduruyor
Bir süre sonra fark ediyorsunuz ki Paller sadece yanınızda savaşan, çalışan veya üs içerisinde size yardım eden yaratıklar değil. Aynı zamanda insan doğasının bazı karanlık taraflarını temsil eden birer araç haline geliyorlar.

Ve belki de oyunun en güzel taraflarından biri burada ortaya çıkıyor:

İlk bakışta yalnızca farklı oyun türlerinin bir araya getirilmesinden oluşan karmaşık bir yapı gibi görünen Palworld, biraz derine indiğinizde insan doğası, yozlaşma ve sahip olduğumuz zaaflar üzerine düşündüren bir dünyaya dönüşüyor.

Palworld benim için bu noktada oldukça ilginç bir deneyime dönüştü. Erken erişimde oynayıp “her şeyi hatalı” diyerek bıraktığım bir oyunun, 1.0 sürümünde karşıma bu kadar farklı ve oturmuş bir şekilde çıkması, stüdyonun oyuna ne kadar ciddi yaklaştığını gösterdi.

Elbette Palworld kusursuz değil. Başka oyunlardan aldığı veya fazlasıyla benzetilen mekanikleri hâlâ tartışılabilir. Fakat bir oyunu değerlendirirken yalnızca parçalarının nereden geldiğine bakmak yerine, bu parçaların bir araya getirildiğinde nasıl bir bütün oluşturduğuna da bakmak gerekiyor.

Ve Palworld, farklı türlerden aldığı fikirleri bir araya getirerek bunları kendi dünyası içerisinde birbirini tamamlayan sistemlere dönüştürmeyi başarmış.

Benim açımdan ise en büyük sürpriz, erken erişimde eleştirdiğim oyunun bugün bana bir ayda 300 küsur saat oynatmış olması.

Sanırım bazen bir oyuna ikinci bir şans vermek gerekiyor.

This is largely a neutral review. 

So, you saw the youtube videos, the jokes, memes, artwork and so on. Here are the things you wouldn't know by now.

* If you played craftopia this is largely the same game. In fact I seemed to even recognize some of the assets. Though most people haven't ever heard of craftopia. 
* This is not a chill game. It can be very brutal andexhausting. 
* Base building is not optional. The game strongly forces you to settle down somewhere, and then babysit this tiny piece of land cramming more and more machinery and harvesting more resources for it.
* Speaking of which, I played base building (factorio, satisfactory, conan exiles, space engineers, no man's sky, and others), Palworld lacks things here. Existing mechanics are bare bones and so is pal control. For example, there are lazy workarounds. If a pall can't path to a goal, the game just drops the pal in the middle of a base. Sometimes they stand on top of stations, or interact with them at large distance, and so on.
* Automation lacks a lot of QoL features. Control over employed pals is not great, you can't queue multi-step item construction, etc.
* Combat in the game is mostly fighting turrets. Every pal is a turret which will spam homing projectiles, giant beams, AOEs and so on. There are also "meme beams" you've seen on youtube, those shoot through obstacles. They're very real. 
* Around level 30 game begins to slow down where crafting begins taking too much time. By level 50 it becomes unbearable. For example, I tried to honestly craft "Pal Metal" armol, it took 3 hours for involved pal to just refine it, and it was level 5 kindling.
* Then comes expensive structures which can take more than 30 to 60 minutes to build, unless you invested into work speed, then it'll be five to ten minutes of staring at the timer countdouwn while it is building.
* Then there's crafting of higher tier spheres and ammunition. The higher is item's rank, the longer it takes to build, to make it faster you need better Pals, but to get those pals you need better spheres.
* Some weapon progression is very weird, higher tier rifle can deal less damage than a muskets while also using more expensive ammo.
* So all things considered, the fastest way to defeat some boss is to spam spheres or overlevel the boss by 10 levels or so. Which obviously does not work when you hit the level cap or when the boss is immune to capture.
* You also don't get xp from killing, only from capturing 5 kinds of monsters, defeating bosses for the first time and unlocking teleportation points. So by level 50 you'll be combing the map for creatures, bosses, etc you missed.
* All those activities seem to be perfectly spaced to get you to next level after you do them N times, which makes me wonder why have xp at all. 
* Level difference is insurmountable. If you're level 30 running into level 60 monster, you can't skill it via combat. Though I guess if by a miracle you somehow got proper sphere, you could trycapturing the monster. 
* There's heavy use of asset store assets for landscape and so on. Pals/monsters have consistent design, but it is often at odds with more realistic world. Quality is not level, some of the base tiles look a lot worse than others. "Poymer" set significantly lacks detail for example.
* The world is very empty. The landscape and landmasses are sculpted and aren't bad, but there are very few landmarks within, and usually it is just roaming identical groups here and there. Could use more visual/etc polish. 
* There is pal breeding. But breeding is gated by time, egg hatching is gated by time, and in order to produce a pall you need cake, which is gated by having to farm even more resources. Compare it to shin megami tensei nocturne, where you could just go, fuse monsters and get result instantly. 
* The game also could use larger variety of combat skills. Monsters reuse attack spells, and there aren't many of them. There's hurled mud, hurled rock, several variations of hurricanes, several types of meme laser beams, some AOEs.... but variety is smaller compared to monster designs. 
 
All of this together creates impression that progression is wrong. As in you are not getting weapons you should've gotten, things arrive too late, they deal too little damage, and maintaining them is too much hassle. 

So beyond level 50 it is a good idea to adjust item settings. Disable equipment decay, for a start, remove death penalty, reduce hunger, maybe increase regeneration outside of combat. Near the end of the games the bosses have nintendo difficulty. With final bosses it is nintendo difficulty cubed. The main issue here is that there are good and complex systems in the game but they're buried and game never shows them. By the end suddenly elemental vulnerability become important (because you can't outlevel things which hit level cap), but you never used them. Same goes for accessories and so on. Certain bosses require stacking accessories. 

And in addition to to that you might want to use save editor just to give you all the annoying resources so you can just build stuff. Like I said, refining metal for hours just to make an armor (which won't help anyway) is not fun.

Speaking of combat, combat is odd, because while fights are cinematic, The game loves spamming AOEs that are far too large to dodge, and just has areas where AOE just covers everything mid-fight. 

Having said that the developer definitely played their cards right with this. Used craftopia as prototype, and got all the money from people who were hungry for alternative monster game content.

Если описывать совсем просто, то это как Genshin Impact, только с полноценным выживанием, строительством базы и коллекционированием существ. Исследуешь огромный красочный мир, находишь новые локации, сражаешься с боссами и постоянно отвлекаешься от основной цели, потому что где-то вдали заметил интересного Пала. Только здесь за красивыми существами не нужно лезть в гачу: увидел, победил, поймал и забрал себе.

Палы не просто бегают рядом и участвуют в сражениях. На них можно путешествовать по земле, воде и воздуху, а у многих есть собственное оружие или полезные способности. Одни добывают руду, другие выращивают растения, поливают грядки, производят электричество или помогают создавать предметы. Поэтому хочется ловить не только самых сильных и красивых, но и тех, кто пригодится для развития базы.

Коллекционирование отлично связано со всеми остальными механиками. Каждый новый Пал может открыть дополнительную возможность в бою, ускорить производство или просто стать удобным транспортом. Потом начинается разведение, поиск редких особенностей и создание почти идеальных существ. Я эти вообще занимался почти весь end game игры, чтобы вывести топ палов около часов 40.

Здесь есть добыча ресурсов, крафт, строительство, оружие, броня, голод и постепенное развитие технологий. При этом выживание не превращается в бесконечное рубление одного дерева. Со временем большую часть рутины можно автоматизировать: строишь плантации и фабрики, распределяешь Палов по рабочим местам и наблюдаешь, как база начинает жить самостоятельно.
Особенно хорошо работает само исследование мира. Постоянно находишь подземелья, редких Палов, опасные территории, новых боссов и ресурсы для следующего этапа развития. Получил летающего Пала, и уже знакомые места раскрываются с другой стороны. Сделал более мощное оружие, и можно отправляться туда, где раньше тебя уничтожали за несколько секунд. Игра почти всегда даёт причину сделать ещё один небольшой шаг, который незаметно превращается в несколько часов.

В кооперативе всё это работает ещё лучше. Можно вместе исследовать мир, строить огромную базу, распределять обязанности, охотиться на боссов или наблюдать, как друг случайно начинает войну со всей местной охраной. Здесь достаточно занятий и для любителей сражений, и для строителей, и для тех, кто готов часами собирать полную коллекцию Палов.

Palworld объединяет открытый мир, выживание, строительство, автоматизацию и коллекционирование существ в одну невероятно затягивающую игру. Все механики дополняют друг друга, поэтому практически любое действие помогает дальнейшему развитию. Поймал нового Пала, улучшил базу, открыл технологию, победил босса и отправился исследовать следующую область.

Tras haber superado las 1.000 horas de juego y haber presenciado la evolución del título desde sus etapas tempranas hasta su versión final 1.0, resulta evidente que Palworld es algo más que la suma de sus memes virales iniciales. Pocketpair ha logrado consolidar una propuesta que fusiona con notable solidez la recolección y crianza de criaturas con mecánicas avanzadas de supervivencia, automatización de bases y combate de acción en tiempo real.
No estamos ante una experiencia impecable, pero sí ante un título ambicioso, enormemente adictivo y estructurado de forma que recompensa tanto la dedicación diaria como la planificación estratégica a largo plazo.

Puntos fuertes
•	Bucle de juego y automatización profundo:
El verdadero corazón de Palworld a largo plazo radica en la gestión de bases y la especialización de las criaturas (Pals). La sinergia entre las aptitudes de trabajo de cada especie y las líneas de producción avanzadas ofrece una sensación de progreso constante. Optimizar cadenas de recolección, minería, agricultura y manufactura es sumamente gratificante.
•	Sistema de crianza e ingeniería genética:
Para los jugadores apasionados por la optimización de atributos (endgame), el sistema de reproducción es uno de los apartados más sólidos. La selección sistemática de pasivas y la transmisión de habilidades permiten diseñar composiciones de equipo verdaderamente únicas, lo que justifica por sí solo cientos de horas de contenido técnico.
•	Exploración y progresión de combate:
El mapa ofrece una escala respetable con una distribución vertical bien resuelta gracias al uso de monturas terrestres, acuáticas y aéreas. El combate, respaldado por la variedad de armamento del jugador y la interacción activa de las habilidades de los Pals, mantiene una dinámica ágil tanto en incursiones de mazmorras como en los enfrentamientos contra jefes de torre.
•	Flexibilidad de servidor y multijugador:
La capacidad de ajustar minuciosamente los parámetros del mundo (tasas de captura, tiempos de eclosión, daño, desgaste de recursos) permite adaptar la experiencia tanto para sesiones en solitario como para servidores comunitarios competitivos o cooperativos.

Aspectos a considerar y margen de mejora
•	Inteligencia artificial y pathfinding en bases:
Aunque la versión 1.0 ha mitigado significativamente los cuellos de botella respecto al lanzamiento en acceso anticipado, la IA de los Pals aún experimenta fallos puntuales en la asignación automática de tareas o en la navegación por construcciones multinivel complejas. Requiere que el jugador diseñe bases relativamente despejadas para evitar problemas de ruta.
•	Curva de contenido en la fase final (Endgame):
Superado el nivel máximo y habiendo optimizado las cadenas de producción principales, el juego depende en gran medida del interés del usuario por la crianza perfecta, los jefes de Incursión (Raids) y la superación de desafíos autoimpuestos. Si disfrutas de la optimización de recursos, la exploración de mundos abiertos y la crianza meticulosa, este juego ofrece un valor por hora invertida difícil de igualar en el catálogo actual de Steam.

Palworld starts out as a genuinely enjoyable experience. The early game feels fresh, creative, and full of energy. The open world is fun to explore, the environments feel alive, and catching new Pals is exciting. The survival mechanics are simple but satisfying, and the base building system gives you a sense of progress without overwhelming you. For a while, the game strikes a perfect balance between exploration, crafting, and discovery. You feel like you are constantly moving forward, unlocking new Pals, expanding your base, and learning new systems. The early hours are easily the strongest part of the game.

As you push deeper into the crafting system, the experience begins to change. The moment you start working on heavier items like guns, advanced machinery, and high tier crafting stations, the workload increases dramatically. Even with a full base of Pals helping, the amount of resources required becomes unreal. You spend long stretches gathering materials, waiting for production to finish, and managing workstations, but the payoff never matches the effort. The progression stops feeling like survival and starts feeling like a grind fest.

The struggle becomes even more obvious when you begin spending rare resources. Ore, ancient civilization cores, and high tier parts are required for almost everything in the mid and late game. Ore fuels nearly every crafting recipe, including ammo, metal parts, machinery, and upgrades. Ancient civilization cores are needed for powerful gear and advanced stations. High tier parts are required for weapons and late game equipment. All of these resources are extremely time consuming to gather, and even with Pals supporting you, the process feels slow and repetitive. You end up spending more time farming the same resource nodes than exploring the world or enjoying the creative systems that made the early game so fun.

The disappointment becomes even stronger once you finally craft guns. You invest a huge amount of time gathering rare materials, building the required stations, and grinding for ore, but the weapons feel weak once you use them. After all that work, they do not deliver the power or satisfaction you expect. It feels like the game punishes you for trying to progress. The reward does not match the effort, and the excitement of unlocking new gear fades quickly.

As the game continues, the survival elements become less important. Hunger, temperature, and exploration challenges fade into the background. Instead, the entire experience becomes centered around resource farming. Ore becomes the core of the mid game. Ancient civilization cores become the gatekeeper for late game progress. High tier parts become the bottleneck for weapons and machinery. The game slowly shifts from a survival adventure into a repetitive grind where you spend more time managing production lines than actually playing in the world.

Palworld shines in its early game with a fun world, great exploration, and a strong gameplay loop. The mid and late game struggle under the weight of the crafting system. The grind becomes overwhelming, the rewards feel underpowered, and the pacing loses its momentum. The balance between effort and reward collapses, and the excitement of discovery is replaced by long stretches of repetitive farming. Palworld has incredible potential and an amazing start, but the heavy crafting requirements and resource grind take away a lot of the enjoyment once you reach the deeper stages of the game.

[h2]良かったところ[/h2]
[h2]◆様々な良作のこうだったら良いなを上手く詰められている[/h2]
ポ〇モンに似てると言われてますが、むしろゼ〇ダやA〇Kのが近く、それらが上手く合わさっていると感じました。

寝る前に少し拠点を整備するか～って思うと、大抵数時間は過ぎてます。
色々な事ができるため、歯止めが本当に効かなくなりますね。

近年の某ポ〇モンやモ〇スターズは個性付けのためか奇抜な見た目や性格、思想の人間キャラ（しかも仲間やライバル）が増えており、正直遊んでいてキツいと思う事が多々あるのですが、こちらはその辺りが強くなく、パルを可愛がる方に意識を集中しやすくて良かったです。
[strike]気に食わないやつがいてもぶっ飛ばせるのもグッド[/strike]
[h2]◆アプデで初期の欠点が大きく改善されている[/h2]
全部書くと長くなるので割愛しますが、初期の頃より圧倒的に遊びやすくなっています。
こまめにユーザーの声を聞いて改善していってるんだなと思いましたね。
特にレイドボスの虹パッシブ付けが異常に鬼畜だったり、凸がかなり気が遠くなったりというのも改善されてめちゃくちゃ遊びやすくなってます。
アーリーの時は経験値を増やしてないとろくにレベルが上がらない期間がありましたが、それも改善されてます（しかも経験値が増えるという調整よりは要素が増えて必然的に上がりやすくなった感じの調整）。
スタックしやすい問題も正式版では一度も経験してません。

Palworld ist alleine schon wegen seiner Hintergrundgeschichte und der erfolgreichen rechtlichen Auseinandersetzung mit Nintendo ein Kauf wert. Der Preis ist auch echt günstig im Vergleich zur Konkurrenz.

Nüchtern betrachtet macht Palworld Spaß, aber man merkt schon, dass es keine AAA-Produktion ist. Über die paar Grafikbugs, KI-Probleme und recht dünne Story kann ich aber getrost mit Hinblick auf den preis wegsehen. Der Gameloop bestehend in Basis aufbauen, bessere Rüstung/Waffen graften und neue Ressourcen beschaffen (Pals und Rohstoffe) kann einen ziemlich hart in Anspruch nehmen, sodass man manchmal kaum zum Erkunden kommt. Persönlich hätte ich mir da mehr Automation gewünscht. Um zum Beispiel KI-Kerne zu machen muss man ständig anweisen die Zwischenprodukte herzustellen, man ist also gegen Ende leider elend lange am Mikromanagen. Zum Beispiel haben mir im späteren Verlauf die Balls gefehlt, ich konnte immer nur diese GiGa-Balls machen, die echt nutzlos waren. Deswegen musste ich mich mehr auf die Basis konzentrieren um Balls einer brauchbaren Qualitätsstufe zu bekommen. Als ich dann endlich die Balls hatte konnte ich zum vorletzten Gebiet aufbrechen.  

Der Schwierigkeitsgrad ist echt sehr seltsam, aber ich kann persönlich damit leben. Die Hauptstory ist die meiste Zeit Superleicht, alles was danach kommt ist lächerlich schwer. Also als Spieler, der sich schon gut vorbereitet, aber nicht irgendwelche Meta-Teams baut, sondern halt eins mit Pals die cool findet, Ist es ziemlich erschreckend wie Auf was für ein anderes Level plötzlich die End-Game-Herausforderungen sind. Also eher was für Leute, die nach perfekten Pals und perfekten Synergy-Teams streben.

Zu gute Letzt möchte ich nochmal betonen, dass man im Gegensatz zur Konkurrenz hier nur einmal zahlen muss und das komplette Spiel mit allen Pals bekommt. Bei anderen Kauft man sich vielleicht ne gelbe Edition und da bekommt man nicht alle 151 Monster. Nee man brauch noch ein zweites Gerät und dann halt noch Linkkabel, blaue Edition und rote Edition und wird von Nintendo als Teenager so richtig ausgenommen. Man wurden wir damals über den Tisch gezogen, nur um alle Inhalte zu bekommen, aber ich schweife ab.

Palworld macht Spaß, aber kann auch mal in Arbeit ausarten, da Quality of Live Features fehlen. Zum Glück kann man, aber auch in den Welteneinstellungen Änderungen vornehmen um dem entgegenzuwirken. In diesen Single-Player-Spiel begrüße ich das, auch dass die Entwickler einen auch während des Spiels so mit einfachen hinweisen auch drauf hinweisen um sich die Erfahrung ein wenig angenehmer zu machen. 

Am Ende mochte ich die Zeit und auch meine Pals und manche sind mir ans Herz gewachsen oder halt dann Situationen wie Grizzbolt pennt auf dem Stromgenerator und Sekmeht auf meiner hochwertigen Aufbewahrungstruhe usw.

Aufgrund des üppigen Umfangs und dem vergleichsweise günstigen Preis schaue ich über die paar Fehler und Schwächen hinweg und gebe ihm 8 von 10 Balls.

Palworld isn’t just a game—it’s a whole different kind of experience. I’ve played survival games before, both standard ones and more unique ones. But when I played this one, I really, truly never expected it to be this addictive. 
There were very, very few moments in the game where I got bored—what I mean is, there are so many systems and elements that keep you immersed that you don’t even have time to think about getting bored. 
I started playing this game after the 1.0 major update, and it took me about 110 hours to finish it. Yes, it took that long. If you’re wondering why it took so long, let me address that minor issue of boredom: the problem of excessive repetition—which, of course, is common in most games, but I felt it more strongly here. So, someone looking for a survival game with simple, easy mechanics might reach the refund section before even hitting the two-hour mark, and that’s hardly surprising. Well, aside from that issue, I’d say there aren’t any other problems. There’s no point in dragging this out too much.
It’s a next-generation survival game with great optimization, a storyline that’s a real treat, and pals so sweetie you’ll never get enough of them.
Since I’ve clocked in about 110 hours playing solo, you must have a blast playing with friends—it’s pure fun.

176.7 小时。大概有 40 小时是在 2024 年贝菈诺娃、贝菈露洁刚出来那阵子玩的，剩下的一百多小时则是最近重新开档从头玩了一遍。

时隔这么久重新回来，其实会发现《幻兽帕鲁》的核心循环并没有发生什么本质变化：

探索地图 → 抓帕鲁 → 培养帕鲁 → 建基地 → 获取资源 → 解锁更高级的设施 → 抓更强的帕鲁 → 获取更高级的资源 → 挑战更难的塔主和 Boss。

说白了，重复度其实并不低。

但问题在于——它就是挺好玩的。

《幻兽帕鲁》经常被人说是“缝合怪”，但我觉得它真正厉害的地方恰恰就在这个“缝合”上。抓宠、开放世界探索、生存建造、自动化经营、育种培养、第三人称战斗，这些东西单独拿出来都不算新鲜，但它并不是把各种热门玩法生搬硬套到一起，而是真的知道每套系统里什么东西有趣，然后取其精华，把它们组合成了一个非常顺畅的循环。

尤其是多人模式。

我很幸运，2024 年陪我一起玩这款游戏的朋友，到现在居然还愿意和我一起重新开档。两年过去，游戏更新了很多东西，但最好玩的事情其实还是和以前一样：几个人一起跑图、第一次看到没见过的帕鲁就冲过去抓、一起围殴 Boss、研究接下来该去哪里。

对多人游戏来说，我觉得这反而是最难得的地方。

基地经营方面，我一直是前期“能跑就行”的类型，流水线只要能正常产出东西就懒得折腾，等到后期真正实现物资自由，再慢慢规划基地。看着采集、搬运、生产、发电、做饭全部自动运行起来确实非常爽。

不过建造系统也是我认为目前最应该继续改进的部分。

最让我无法理解的一点，就是箱子和很多家具不能直接移动。摆错一个箱子，想挪两米？不好意思，拆掉，东西重新搬出来，然后再造一次。

这不是难度，这是搬家模拟器。

尤其是后期基地规模越来越大的时候，这种毫无意义的重复搬运真的很消磨耐心。我很希望以后地板、家具和建筑组件都能加入更自由的六轴微调，包括平移、旋转和高度调整。因为等玩家真正毕业以后，建造本身完全可以成为另一个长期玩法，而现在的系统多少还是限制了这方面的发挥空间。

养成系统也是类似的问题。

刷词条、育种、配种、升星、强化、重复刷 Boss，到大后期肯定会越来越重复。哪怕我的存档已经调得相当休闲，有时候材料需求还是能把人逼到不得不稍微借助一点……帕鲁世界之外的神秘力量。

不过对我来说倒也还能接受，因为我的目标本来就是全成就和尽可能全收集。既然选择当收集癖，有些牢还是得自己坐。

难度方面我觉得整体控制得不错。普通内容基本不会给人太大的压力，真正开始有挑战的主要还是后期那些究极石板 Boss 和高难塔主。既不会让普通玩家前期寸步难行，也给愿意继续刷装备和培养帕鲁的人留了一些目标。

玩到 176 个小时以后，我当然不会说它没有问题。核心循环重复，后期培养很肝，建造系统还有不少可以改善的地方。

但如果一款游戏能让我在两年后重新开档，再从零开始跑一遍几乎相同的循环，而且还能让我觉得“再抓一只、再升一级、再造一个东西就睡”，那它显然还是做对了很多事情。

更难得的是，当年一起玩的那群人，现在还在。

可能这才是我对《幻兽帕鲁》最好的评价。

Two games, one review, because Palworld took Conan Exiles apart, kept the good half, and left the suffering in the box.

Survival. Conan gives you thirst, hunger, heat, cold and corruption. The desert is trying to kill you before anything holding a sword gets its turn. Palworld gives you a mild sense of peckishness and weather that a coat solves. Eat a berry. One of these is a survival game; the other keeps a food bar out of politeness.

Labour. Conan: you club a man unconscious, tie a rope to him, drag him across the desert to a machine called the Wheel of Pain, and starve him until he agrees to run your forge. Palworld: you throw a ball at something and it smiles while it runs your forge. Identical system. Only one of them tells you what it is.

Breeding. Conan asks you to camp a spawn point for hours until a named blacksmith shows up. Palworld asks you to run a stud farm with inheritance charts and trait rerolls. Neither is a hobby you should describe out loud at work.

Hauling. Palworld gives you a creature whose entire purpose is carrying ore from the rock to the box while you do something else. Conan's most advanced logistics technology is your own back.

Automation. Palworld's base is an idle game wearing survival clothes, and it works, because idle games understood what an evening is worth long before survival games did. Conan has no automation whatsoever, and treats this as a personality trait.

Building. Conan has snap points, stability rules, material tiers and a decay timer that deletes your house if you take a holiday. Palworld snaps, stays, and never punishes you for having a life outside it. Conan's system is deeper and it is also the reason your clanmate quit.

Death. Conan drops everything you own exactly where you died, which is always at the bottom of a slope with a crocodile on it. Palworld takes a little and shrugs.

Other people. Conan's social contract is that someone will eventually blow up your house while you sleep, and there is a scheduled window for it. Palworld's is that your friend logged in and rearranged the chests. One of these produces stories. The other produces evenings.

Traversal. Palworld folded movement into the capture system, so your mount, your glider and your artillery are all the same animal. It's the single most elegant idea either game has had, and Conan answered it with horses.

Combat. Conan is heavy, stamina-bound, occasionally magnificent and frequently a man falling through the floor. Palworld is a perfectly competent third-person shooter that happens to have a monster on your shoulder holding a rifle.

Endgame. Conan's is an avatar of a god the size of a keep stamping on somebody's fort at a scheduled hour, plus whatever the neighbours are quietly building. Palworld's is a tower with a boss in it, a health bar and a timer, and then the next tower. One is an event that happens to a community. The other is something you beat on a Tuesday and never think about again.

Setting. Conan has Robert E. Howard's world, and the weight comes through even the jank. Palworld is pleasant, tidy and gone from your head by morning. Cozy is not a setting, it's a temperature.

Money. Conan runs a Bazaar and a battle pass, and then hands you an entire engine upgrade for nothing. Palworld shipped years of free updates from a studio that spent the same years being sued over throwing a ball at an animal. Nintendo's claim, the one that frightened an industry, comes to roughly the price of a used hatchback.

Two notes for Funcom that nobody asked for.

Sorcery should never have been handed to the player. In Howard, magic is what the villain has and the hero doesn't: foreign, decadent, and always paid for by someone else. Turning it into a skill tree flattens the one thing that separated this world from every other fantasy setting on the shelf. Keep sorcery, make it terrifying, and keep it on the far side of the sword.

And the followers. One thrall at your heel isn't a warband, it's a man with a job. Let the posse grow, and then let the settlement behave like one: people who move, eat, argue, and have somewhere to be at dusk. Palworld's camp is dumber than Conan's in every respect except this one, and it's the respect that counts, because the pals look like they live there and your thralls look like furniture with health bars.

The future, which is the actual point. Palworld won the convenience argument so completely that Conan can't compete there and shouldn't try. What's left to Funcom is everything Palworld declined to take: the cruelty, the weight, the world with an author's name on it. Conan Enhanced answered with Unreal 5, both maps on one character, and mods on day one, which is the right instinct aimed at the wrong organ. Prettier is not the differentiator. Harsher is. Meanwhile Palworld shipped 1.0 with a rewritten story, and it's still watery. That's the joke: the cozy one is annexing ground Conan never bothered to defend, and doing it badly, while Conan says more with nobody talking at all. Sun directly overhead, music rising over an empty horizon, your only weapon snapping two swings into a fight you picked. Nothing is narrated. Everything is told.

Two thumbs up, and not polite ones. Pocketpair built the most generous version of this genre anyone has managed, and did it while being sued over the shape of a ball. Funcom kept an eight-year-old game standing and then rebuilt it in a newer engine rather than selling it back to you twice.

Two games about capturing living things and putting them to work. One is honest about it. The other is winning. Neither of them needs to copy the other's homework.

Funcom, last thing: be braver. You own the cruellest world in the genre and you keep sanding the edges off it. Nobody is going to out-comfort Palworld. Go all the way in, or go down doing it.

Signed, your unpaid publisher.

This was a great early access game. This is an awful fully-released game.

The core gameplay loop and exploration is quite fun, and the game has that property of always derailing you when you start a task because something shows up — something I overall consider both good and hard to do well.

This is kind of where the praise stops. The fact that the game was released in this state feels very odd to me. There are so, so, SO MANY *obvious* QoL improvements that the game is missing and just weird design choices: 

From the Palpedia and box and storage not being searchable, the box and storage requiring you to either move each Pal individually or send your whole box to storage, the fact you only have 3 different locks for sorting, the fact you can't queue crafting, the fact that the expedition requires you to have 100 Pals in your box and not your storage with you at all times, the fact that the only way to find out what status effects do is by reading the survival journal entry about it roughly 3/4ths the way down the list, the way you can't really see what status effects a Pal has other than one, the way that you can't properly configure chests to only be deposited into or withdrawn from, the way chest item filter categories are so ridiculously imbalanced (with hundreds of items just being categorised as "Pal materials"), the way the game expects you to do well over 50 arena runs if you want all achievements but there is no "fight again" option and they even place you looking away from the door after the fight (and you need to go through 2 loading screens for each fight, and only 1 of the cutscenes are skippable, so I literally spent 46s in loading or cutscenes and 3–7s in the actual fight per rotation), the way that the Ancient Refinery requires you to manually turn it on every time even though it is literally in the final tier of  production machinery, the fact that completing the Palpedia or beating all the hardmode raids is not an achievement but doing the arena well over 50 times is, the fact that the most expensive Arena Ticket items require you to have almost 100 wins on the higher difficulties and yet those items are extremely outdated by that point... I could keep going. 

This game is mindboggingly poorly and weirdly designed, even though it has had millions of players playing it for years in Early Access — they had the best playtesting feedback volume a company could ask for, and yet the game feels as if the devs haven't even played it themselves. This game has the monetary backing of a giant in Sony Entertainment, and yet they couldn't polish it at all? I didn't even mention the god-awful multiplayer performance, with the host having a huge specs load while the other players suffer terrible consequences for even mild ping.

Palworld had all the hype, potential, and opportunity to deliver something amazing in their 1.0 release. However, this is mostly just a shame — an unpolished, poorly-designed mess.

- the skills system
- the passive/pal ability system

- pals will put things in the first chest they find, regardless of if they are already in a chest

- has next to no automation capability. all crafting MUST be started by the player
- multiplayer isn't that fun since XP and technology unlocks are not shared, so if one player gets ahead, its impossible to catch up reasonably

- resources required in the endgame is far too grind-y. repeated raid boss fights/long expeditions to get AI Cores

目前我的评价主要建立在单人战役体验上。如果后续官方对剧情或相关内容进行较大幅度的修改和改善，我可能会重新考虑并修改这条评论。

I have only played the bo7 single-player campaign, so this review is based entirely on the campaign experience.

First, the positives: the gunplay feels quite good. The shooting feedback is solid, and the hit and kill feedback is satisfying. The actual combat can still be quite enjoyable. The campaign is also fairly long, and the environments and visual presentation are impressive in many parts.

However, the biggest problem is the story.

The story feels extremely disappointing to me. The overall narrative feels disconnected from the traditional Call of Duty and Black Ops identity. While playing, it was difficult to feel the same tension and immersion that I associate with previous Call of Duty campaigns. There are plenty of long and beautifully designed sequences, but impressive visuals cannot make up for the problems with the actual story.

If I judge the game purely on its gunplay, shooting mechanics, and kill feedback, I can still give it a positive review. However, when the single-player campaign is considered as a whole, the story makes it difficult for me to recommend it without reservations.

My current opinion is based entirely on the single-player campaign. If the developers make significant changes or improvements to the story and related content in the future, I may reconsider and update this review.

Overall: Great gunplay and satisfying kill feedback, with impressive visuals and environments, but the extremely weak story seriously hurts the single-player campaign.

Call of Duty remains the industry benchmark for fast-paced, arcade-style first-person shooters, offering unmatched gunplay, fluid movement mechanics, and polished cinematic campaigns. The multiplayer experience is consistently engaging, supported by robust weapon customization and a steady flow of seasonal content, while modes like *Warzone* deliver high-intensity battle royale action.

However, the franchise has notable drawbacks. The annual release cycle often leads to iterative rather than truly innovative updates, occasional map design inconsistencies, and aggressive monetization strategies through battle passes and cosmetic microtransactions. Large file sizes and occasional balancing issues can also detract from the overall experience.

Overall, *Call of Duty* is a top-tier choice for players seeking crisp gun mechanics and thrilling, quick-match multiplayer, even if the yearly formula occasionally feels routine.
