# New World — A Great MMO That Never Got the Chance It Deserved

I started playing **New World** about a month or two after launch, so I was there during those early days when the game was far from perfect. There were bugs everywhere, the game had plenty of negative reviews, and some of the issues were genuinely frustrating. I still remember the Trading Post constantly going down in the beginning — something that could make simple buying and selling feel like a chore.

But despite all of that, I genuinely enjoyed this game.

Over time, Amazon did make the game more stable, and underneath all the problems was something that I honestly believe was special: **one of the best MMO experiences I have ever had.**

For me, the MMO aspect of New World was incredible.

Running dungeons with other players, organising server-wide chest runs, meeting up at arranged times for raids and expeditions, working together with guild members, and simply talking to people from all over the world — those are the things I will remember.

It wasn't just about getting better gear.

It was about the people you met along the way.

I have spoken to players from all over the world through this game. People who started as complete strangers would end up running content together regularly, helping each other, crafting for each other and just having a great time. Those experiences created memories, and that is something a lot of games fail to achieve.

I was mostly a PvE player myself. I spent a huge amount of time working towards having the gear and builds needed for the different dungeons and mutations. I enjoyed playing both DPS and tank, and there was something extremely satisfying about being able to jump into different mutations and know that you had put the work in to be properly prepared.

The progression systems were another part of New World that I really enjoyed.

The trade skills, crafting, buying and selling items, and working your way towards those higher milestones gave you plenty of things to work towards outside of combat. I remember how satisfying it was reaching Grandmaster and earning the title after putting so much time into those skills.

And crafting for guild mates when you had all of your crafting buffs active?

That was genuinely fun.

It made the game feel like a community rather than just a collection of individual players.

The mounts were also a great addition, although I do think they arrived far too late. Having them earlier would have made travelling around Aeternum much more enjoyable, but when they finally arrived, they were a welcome addition.

I also think the PvE and PvP balance was actually in a pretty good place overall. There was room for improvement, of course, but the game had a good foundation.

Personally, I would have loved to see something similar to a **Dark Zone-style area** added — somewhere where PvP was always enabled and everyone knew exactly what they were walking into. A high-risk, high-reward area where you could lose something by pushing your luck. Something like that could have added a completely different level of tension and excitement to the world.

And then there is the biggest problem New World had.

**The bugs.**

I genuinely believe this is what destroyed the game's potential.

New World had an incredible foundation, but when a game launches with serious bugs, exploits and game-breaking problems, players lose confidence. Once the player base starts leaving, it becomes incredibly difficult to recover, especially for an MMO that depends on having a healthy population.

You can have a fantastic world.

You can have great combat.

You can have enjoyable PvE and PvP.

You can have crafting, trading, progression, guilds and an amazing community.

But if players constantly encounter bugs that break the game, eventually they stop coming back.

That is the lesson I hope is taken from New World.

Because honestly, **I would love to see this game come back someday.**

Not necessarily exactly as it was, but something built from the same foundation — taking everything that worked and fixing everything that didn't.

If there ever is a remake, reboot or spiritual successor, I would also love to see Amazon take inspiration from long-running MMOs such as RuneScape when it comes to the way players interact with the wider game world.

I don't think players should necessarily be locked into a single server forever. A more global Trading Post would be fantastic, and having more globally connected instances and activities could help keep the world populated and make it easier for players to find groups.

The MMO should feel like one massive community rather than dozens of separate communities that happen to exist beside each other.

I was playing New World heavily right up until the console launch, and seeing the game eventually reach the point where it is now — with its closure coming in 2027 — is genuinely heartbreaking.

It's strange to think that a game can occupy so much of your time, introduce you to people from all over the world, give you goals to work towards and create memories that stay with you, only for it eventually to disappear.

**New World wasn't a perfect game. Far from it.**

But I don't think it deserved to be remembered simply as a failed MMO.

I remember the dungeon runs.

I remember the chest runs.

I remember organising groups.

I remember crafting gear for guild mates.

I remember grinding skills and finally hitting those big milestones.

I remember the people.

And most importantly, I remember having fun.

That is what I will take away from New World.

There was a genuinely great MMO buried inside this game, and I still believe that.

If Amazon ever decides to take everything they learned from New World and build another MMO from that foundation — **please, for the love of everything, launch it properly and don't let the bugs destroy it.**

Fix the technical problems. Listen to the community. Keep the fantastic combat and progression. Keep the social aspects. Keep the feeling of working together with hundreds of other players.

Give it the time it needs.

Because I would absolutely play it again.

**Thank you, New World, for the memories.**

It is genuinely sad to see you go.

When I finished Black Myth: Wukong, I just sat on the main menu for a while. I knew the game was over, but for some reason, I didn't feel like closing it right away. It was a strange feeling, like something I'd spent so much time working toward had suddenly come to an end.

When I first started playing, the visuals and combat were what impressed me the most. The world looks absolutely beautiful, and the enemy designs are on another level. Some of the bosses drove me completely crazy, but finally beating them made all the frustration worth it. 

The more I played, the more I realized that these weren't the only things I loved about the game.

There was something about this world that kept making me want to explore. Sometimes I'd completely ignore the objective and just walk around, taking in the scenery. I'd stop in the mountains, in front of an old temple, or next to a quiet river just to listen to the music for a while.

Even the little moments somehow stayed with me. A character you only meet for a short time, a place you find by taking a different path, or a story you weren't expecting to come across... Somehow, those moments can stick in your head for much longer than you'd expect.

And the bosses...

I died to some of them more times than I'd like to admit. After a few attempts, I'd honestly start thinking, "How the hell am I supposed to beat this bosses?" Then I'd try again, learn their moves, die again, and go right back in. :D

But when I finally won, it genuinely felt like I had earned it.

The game only gives you a victory message on the screen, but you know how many times you had to fail before getting there. I think that's one of the biggest things Wukong made me feel: every defeat meant I had learned something new.

There were plenty of moments when I wanted to give up, but somehow I always ended up trying one more time. And when that "one more try" finally worked, it felt like much more than simply making progress in a game.

When I finished Wukong, I wasn't just left with a beautiful game. I was left with bosses I'll remember, places I enjoyed exploring, music that stuck with me, and all those moments where I kept trying until I finally got it right. 

Even though the game is over now, there are still times when I want to go back and spend a little more time in that world.

Maybe that's one of the best things a game can leave you with. Not just the memory of finishing it, but the feeling that, for a while, you were actually part of that world.

五百年的思想改造，十四年的基层历练，八十一场绩效考核，一张西天颁发的编制证书。曾经那个喊着皇帝轮流做的齐天大圣，终于意识到，皇帝是不可能轮流做的，最多轮流做皇帝的保安。
如来对此很满意。
毕竟，能把造反派培养成劳动模范，才是一个成熟管理体系的最高成就。
不过，这只猴子后来似乎又想明白了什么。
于是，我花了两百多块钱，替他重新想了一遍。

游戏开始，我是一只没有名字的猴子。
我对此非常满意。
没有名字，就不用填写家庭住址、毕业院校和五年职业规划。没有学历，就不必担心天庭招聘时要求硕士起步。没有父母，就没人问我什么时候考上弼马温。
一位老猴子告诉我，只要集齐大圣的六根，就能找回曾经的齐天大圣。
我觉得他说得很有道理。
现实中，一个人只要失去了脊梁，通常就能得到很多东西；而在游戏里，一只猴子必须找回六根，才能重新拥有自己。
这说明游戏制作组对现实的理解相当深刻。
我欣然上路。
没走多远，就遇到一个大头和尚。
他什么也没说，只是走过来把我拍死了。
我觉得这位和尚很有修养。
现实中的某些人，在打死你之前，还要先告诉你这是为了你好。他至少省略了谈话环节。
死了几次以后，我终于打败了他。
游戏告诉我，我获得了他的精魄。
我这才发现，原来一个人的思想和精神是可以在死后被提取、储存、装备和使用的。
这项技术如果能推广到现实，一定会大幅度提高劳动生产率。
领导再也不用担心员工辞职了。

黄风岭有很多老鼠。
它们有的吃人，有的念经，有的当官，有的当了官以后开始念经。
我一开始分不清它们。
后来发现根本没有必要。
反正都会打我。
一只老虎挡在路上，我跟它打了很久。
它出招很快，攻击很凶，动作相当流畅。我死了十几次，逐渐摸清了它的规律。
我发现，老虎之所以厉害，并不是因为它有多聪明，而是因为它的每一次攻击都能造成伤害。
相比之下，现实中的许多老虎甚至不必亲自动手。
它们只需要坐在那里，告诉下面的狼，下个月必须抓到一百只羊。
狼会去找狐狸。
狐狸会去找兔子。
最后，羊死了，兔子加班了，狼完成了指标，狐狸获得了先进工作者称号。
老虎在年终总结上写道：
本年度生态环境持续向好。
我觉得游戏里的老虎还是太善良了。
它至少愿意和我单挑。

一路上，我遇到许多妖怪。
有些妖怪原本是人，有些原本是神，有些原本是畜生。
它们在人间受尽折磨，修炼几百年，终于获得了吃人的资格。
我突然明白，妖怪的奋斗目标和某些人的奋斗目标其实没什么区别。
当年自己被吃的时候，天天喊着反抗。
如今轮到自己吃人了，便觉得这是自然规律。
我杀掉一个妖怪，掉了几百点灵蕴。
我杀掉另一个妖怪，又掉了几百点灵蕴。
游戏鼓励我不断杀戮，因为只要杀得足够多，我就能升级，学会新技能，获得更强的力量。
我觉得这套机制非常符合现实。
只不过现实里杀人越货不叫升级，叫资源整合。
游戏里的妖怪会直接告诉我，它要吃了我。
这一点很不真实。
现实中的妖怪通常会告诉你，它想培养你。

我很喜欢游戏里的土地庙。
每当我死得遍体鳞伤，都可以回到庙前，烧上一炷香，重新站起来。
只要香火还在，就永远有机会重来。
当然，代价是周围被我辛辛苦苦打死的小妖，也会重新复活。
我对此颇有感触。
这个世界有时候就是这样。
你费尽千辛万苦，解决了十几个问题，终于来到一个可以喘口气的地方。
休息一晚，第二天上班。
发现十几个问题又回来了。
土地公公坐在那里，面带微笑。
他说，这是天地运行的规律。
我问他，为什么大妖怪死了不会复活，小妖怪却能无限返工？
他说，大妖怪已经完成了历史使命。
小妖怪还需要继续发光发热。
我觉得天庭的人力资源部门一定很喜欢这个设计。

游戏里有一种法术叫定身术。
它可以让敌人暂时停下来。
这是我最喜欢的技能。
小时候，我希望自己拥有七十二变，可以变成鸟、变成鱼、变成任何东西。
长大以后，我发现七十二变没有那么实用。
变成鸟，要担心被猎人打下来。
变成鱼，要担心被渔夫捞上去。
变成人，还要担心房租、工作和信用卡账单。
还是定身术好。
它至少能让我在敌人无休止的攻击中，获得几秒钟喘息的机会。
可惜现实里没有定身术。
现实里的敌人会一边攻击你，一边要求你保持积极心态。
甚至连你的喘息时间，也要被统计进生产效率。
游戏中的定身术有冷却时间。
现实中的压迫没有。

我后来发现，游戏里有很多空气墙。
远远望去，一片大好河山，青山绿水，古刹残垣，仿佛整个世界都在等待我去探索。
可当我兴冲冲地走过去，却被一堵看不见的墙挡住了。
墙没有形状，没有颜色，没有声音。
它只负责告诉我：
此路不通。
我觉得这是整个游戏最富有现实主义精神的设计。
小时候，大人告诉我，世界是广阔的，只要肯努力，哪里都可以去。
长大以后，我才知道，世界确实很广阔。
但大多数地方都有空气墙。
有的叫门槛，有的叫背景，有的叫关系，有的叫资格审查。
最精妙的空气墙，是让你以为面前根本没有墙。
你撞了几十次，鼻青脸肿，终于开始怀疑自己的能力。
墙却毫发无损。
当然，从游戏设计的角度讲，这些空气墙确实有些恼人。部分场景看起来可以探索，实际上却不能通行，地图引导也不够清晰。有时候我并不是败给了妖怪，而是败给了不知道该往哪里走。
但在我第十次试图翻过一块明明只有膝盖高的石头时，我突然释怀了。
这只猴子当年能一个筋斗翻十万八千里。
现在连一块石头都翻不过去。
可见，编制确实能改变一个人。

有人说，《黑神话：悟空》是一款动作游戏。
我不同意。
它分明是一款心理咨询模拟器。
当我第十次被同一个 Boss 打死，我开始怀疑自己的操作。
第二十次，我开始怀疑自己的智商。
第三十次，我开始怀疑自己为什么要花钱买游戏。
第四十次，我终于打赢了。
我兴奋得站了起来，甚至想给自己鼓掌。
这时，我突然意识到一件事。
我刚刚花了两个小时，克服了一项本来根本不存在的困难。
而且，我还为此付了钱。
制作组把我反复殴打，再给我一点胜利的甜头，我便感激涕零，恨不得再买一份送给朋友。
这套奖励机制简直精妙绝伦。
如果资本家能把它应用到工厂里，工人们每完成一个月的工作，不但不要工资，还会主动购买 DLC，请求老板增加劳动强度。
当然，我依然喜欢它的战斗。
棍法的打击感、招式之间的衔接、法术和变身的搭配，都让我觉得自己确实是在操纵一只有本事的猴子，而不是一根装了发动机的晾衣杆。
那些优秀的 Boss 战尤其令人着迷。
最好的敌人会用一次又一次的失败，逼你理解它的节奏。等你终于看穿它的动作、抓住破绽，打出最后一棍时，胜利带来的快感很难被其他东西替代。
只是偶尔，镜头和判定也会加入敌人的阵营。
这让我对公平竞争有了更深刻的理解。

随着旅途深入，我逐渐发现，这个世界里最值得警惕的，并不是妖怪。
妖怪至少知道自己是妖怪。
真正令人难受的，是那些一本正经谈论慈悲的神佛。
有的妖怪作恶多端，却有来历、有背景、有主人。
有的妖怪只是想活下去，却必须死。
我不禁想起小时候看《西游记》，总觉得孙悟空有些奇怪。
遇到没背景的妖怪，他一棒子打死。
遇到有背景的妖怪，打到一半，总会有个神仙急匆匆赶来。
“大圣，棍下留情！”
然后解释，这是我的坐骑，那是我的童子，这个是我养的宠物，那个是我不小心弄丢的法宝。
孙悟空只好收起金箍棒。
我小时候不理解。
为什么神仙养的妖怪，吃了那么多人，却只要被领回家就没事了？
后来才知道，原来妖怪也分编制内和编制外。
编制外的妖怪叫为祸人间。
编制内的妖怪叫下基层锻炼。
这款游戏最令我喜欢的一点，就是它没有把漫天神佛简单画成慈眉善目的正义化身，也没有把所有妖怪都画成生来该死的恶物。
善恶没有那么整齐。
有时候，一身妖气的东西尚有几分人性，满嘴慈悲的东西却连一丝怜悯也没有。
我越来越觉得，孙悟空当年大闹天宫，或许并不是因为他不懂规矩。
恰恰是因为他太懂了。

当然，游戏并不完美。
有些地图绕得让人怀疑土地公公收了房地产开发商的钱；有些支线藏得太深，错过以后只能翻攻略；有些剧情需要对《西游记》及相关传说有一定了解，否则很容易看得云里雾里。
我也不认为困难本身就等于伟大。
一个 Boss 把玩家打死一百次，并不会自动成为优秀的 Boss。
优秀的战斗应该让人觉得，下一次我能赢。
而不是下一次我能换个游戏。
至于那些精美的场景、古建筑、塑像、壁画和音乐，我反而不想使用什么宏大词汇来夸赞。
它们不需要靠口号证明价值。
当我站在那些残破的寺庙里，听着风声，看着曾经受人膜拜的神佛只剩下斑驳的面孔时，我忽然觉得，游戏里的废墟比许多崭新的宫殿更有生命力。
宫殿喜欢告诉人们，它的主人有多伟大。
废墟只会告诉人们：
主人已经没了。
这一点令我非常欣慰。

我想，这个游戏最有意思的地方，在于它并没有让我扮演孙悟空。
它让我扮演一只想找回孙悟空的猴子。
这两者区别很大。
如果让我直接扮演孙悟空，我只需要战胜敌人。
但让我扮演一只寻找孙悟空的猴子，我便不得不思考一个问题：
我究竟在寻找什么？
是一根能打死所有妖怪的棍子？
是一副刀枪不入的身体？
是齐天大圣的名号？
还是那个曾经敢把金箍棒指向天空的自己？
小时候，我觉得孙悟空最厉害的地方，是他一个筋斗能翻十万八千里。
现在，我觉得他最厉害的地方，是有人告诉他天最大，他偏要拿棍子量一量。
他后来成了佛。
世人都说，这是修成正果。
可我始终想不明白。
一只自由自在的猴子，为什么非得变成一尊供人烧香的佛，才算有了出息？
花果山上，一只猴子摘了个桃子，吃得高高兴兴。
灵山上，一尊佛得到了永恒的供奉，却连挠痒痒都不方便。
究竟谁修成了正果？
我不知道。
但我知道，如果有一天，我成为了齐天大圣，我绝对不会接受斗战胜佛的封号。
不是因为我不喜欢佛。
而是因为我讨厌所有需要别人批准的自由。

所以，我给《黑神话：悟空》好评。
不是因为它出自哪里，不是因为它承载了多少人的期待，也不是因为我必须为某种文化符号鼓掌。
而是因为它确实给了我出色的战斗、令人难忘的美术和音乐，以及一个让我在关掉游戏以后，仍然愿意琢磨的故事。
它让我在屏幕前死了无数次，也让我想起小时候，那个曾经相信一只猴子真能打上凌霄宝殿的自己。
我不知道那只猴子最终有没有找回自由。
至少，我在游戏里还有一个权利。
当神佛喋喋不休的时候，我可以按下跳过。
当妖怪试图吃我的时候，我可以举起棍子。
当整个世界都告诉我应该认命的时候，我还可以点击重新挑战。
现实中，这三个功能都需要解锁。
尤其是最后一个。
最后，感谢游戏科学。
我已经花了几十个小时，打败了无数妖魔鬼怪，经历了数不清的磨难，终于明白了一个道理：
孙悟空被压在五行山下五百年，根本不是因为他打不过如来。
而是因为他始终没有找到存档点。
希望下一部作品能让他找到。
否则，齐天大圣历经千辛万苦，好不容易打碎了头上的金箍，刚想仰天大笑，天上便传来一个声音：
“恭喜您成功通关试用期。请购买季票，解锁真正的自由。”
我低头看了一眼 Steam 账户。
然后默默掏出了钱包。
原来这一路上，最听话的猴子是我。

!!! IMPORTANT: BEFORE PLAYING THIS GAME, LEARN AT LEAST THE BASICS OF SUN WUKONG AND JOURNEY TO THE WEST !!!

I genuinely think people should know this before starting the game. If you know absolutely nothing about Sun Wukong or Journey to the West, there is a good chance you will spend a large part of the game wondering what the hell is going on.

I got almost halfway through the game without fully understanding the story. Who are these characters? Why am I fighting them? What happened in the past? Why are certain characters so important? The game explains a lot of this as if the player is already supposed to know the answers.

Eventually, I literally had to stop playing and research Sun Wukong and Journey to the West online. Only then did many parts of the game start making sense. Black Myth: Wukong isn't simply retelling Wukong's original journey from the beginning; much of its story takes place after the events associated with Journey to the West.

The problem is that the game doesn't do a particularly good job of explaining this to newcomers. It feels like the developers designed the story assuming everyone already knows Chinese mythology, Journey to the West, and Sun Wukong's story. If I have to leave the game and research the source material just to properly understand what the game is trying to tell me, I consider that a serious storytelling problem.

My other major problem is the length.

THIS GAME IS WAY LONGER THAN IT NEEDS TO BE.

And the lack of gameplay variety makes that problem even worse. You basically use the same main weapon, the staff, throughout the entire game. Yes, there are different stances, abilities, spells, and transformations, but for me, none of that replaces the variety that completely different weapon types could have provided.

For a game this long, I would have loved to use different weapon classes. After dozens of hours using the same fundamental combat system, encounters inevitably start feeling similar. The game is already long, and because the core combat doesn't evolve enough, it feels even longer than it actually is.

But one of my biggest problems with the entire game is easily the level design.

Some areas LOOK like you should be able to explore them. There is a perfectly normal-looking path in front of you. No cliff, no wall, no closed gate, no logical environmental reason why you shouldn't be able to continue.

You walk forward.

INVISIBLE WALL.

They literally put invisible walls in the middle of paths that visually look completely accessible.

Even worse, the environment constantly gives you the impression that certain places are explorable. You see a path, naturally follow it because you expect to discover something, and sometimes there is absolutely NOTHING at the end.

No item.

No enemy.

No secret.

No lore.

No reward.

Nothing.

Some areas even look like they should become accessible through a quest or lead somewhere important, but you walk toward them and once again hit an invisible wall.

This completely damages the feeling of exploration. Eventually, instead of thinking, "I wonder what's over there?" you start thinking, "There's probably another invisible wall."

Good level design should visually communicate where the player can and cannot go. If you don't want me going somewhere, put a cliff there. Put a locked gate there. Put rocks there. Put a collapsed building there. Give me ANY environmental reason why I can't continue.

Don't show me a perfectly walkable path and then put an invisible wall in the middle of it.

That's just bad level design.

The dead-end paths make this even more frustrating. The game presents these large environments and side paths as if exploration matters, but sometimes you spend time exploring only to receive absolutely nothing for it. At that point, exploration stops feeling rewarding and starts feeling like wasted time.

And then I learned something AFTER FINISHING THE GAME that annoyed me even more:

THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT ENDINGS.

I followed the main path, finished the game normally, and naturally assumed that the ending I got was the actual conclusion.

Then I discovered there was another ending that required additional content.

Why?

If the other ending provides a more meaningful conclusion to the story, why doesn't simply following the main story naturally lead toward it? Why should I defeat the final boss, finish the game, and then have to search "Black Myth: Wukong true ending" online afterward?

I have nothing against secret or alternative endings. They can be great. But hiding a more meaningful conclusion behind content that players can easily miss just feels unnecessary.

Visually, Black Myth: Wukong is incredible. Some of the boss designs are excellent, the animations are impressive, and the combat can be genuinely fun, especially during the earlier parts of the game.

But great graphics don't erase these problems.

I had to research outside the game to properly understand the story. The game is unnecessarily long. Having essentially one main weapon means the combat doesn't have enough variety to carry that length. The level design constantly gives misleading visual information about where you can explore. There are invisible walls in the middle of completely normal-looking paths. Some paths lead nowhere and reward you with absolutely nothing. And after finishing the game, you can discover that there was another, more meaningful ending you didn't even know existed.

Black Myth: Wukong, for me, is a game with some fantastic ideas and incredible presentation that becomes unnecessarily exhausting because of its design decisions.

And I'll say it again:

!!! BEFORE PLAYING THIS GAME, LEARN AT LEAST THE BASICS OF JOURNEY TO THE WEST AND SUN WUKONG !!!

Otherwise, you might end up like me halfway through the game, searching the internet and asking yourself:

"What the hell am I playing, who are these people, and what is even happening?"

[h1] 凄まじい力作で大作だが、戦闘完成度の部分で色々思う所はある [/h1]

「ボスラッシュ」との評価の通り、最初から最後まで密度の濃いゲームだった。
感心したことに、ボス戦において「またコレかよ！」と感じることはほとんど無く、常に全く新しいボスと闘っている感覚だった。再戦系は心象的に全体の１％も感じず（大蛙とか岩塊みたいな妖怪くらい？）、「使い回しは無い」と言いきってしまっても良いくらいだ。
約100分の1でしかないボスにおいても、凝った魅せる技とモーションが満載で、戦闘前の演出も手抜きがない、「まだ引き出しがあるのか！」と最後まで驚きっぱなしであった。
私は「西遊記」をほとんど知らないのだが、チョイ役で出てきたアイツやアイツも、きっと多くの人に知られているキャラなのだろうと予想できる。それらをこの高品質で制作されれば、そりゃ特に国内からは絶賛しかないよなと納得だ。そして日本人でもわかる、楽して儲けようとか、アイデア流用して大きな規模で作ってやろうとか、そういうゲームではない。製作者の[b] 「凄いゲームを作るんだ！私たちが考える最高の西遊記ゲームを創造するんだ！」 [/b]という高い志を感じた。

 ただここまで大絶賛しておいて何だが、戦闘バランスはすこし納得のいかないものだった。
特に「主人公の怯み」と「敵のスーパーアーマー」にはウンザリさせられた。主人公の攻撃はいわゆるコンボで、5段目が強いのだが、4段目がとにかく貧弱である。例えば筋骨隆々の虎が咆哮しながら突進してきたら「これは怯まない！」と納得できる、スーパーアーマーはゲームバランス的に有っても良いのだ。だが主人公のコンボ4段目はそこらの雑魚すら全く怯ませられない。小柄な弓兵もポコポコ殴られながら平気で矢をつがえ撃ってくるし、裸の虫ですら主人公の4段目など意に介せず斬ってくる。[strike] 綿棒でも振っているのか？ [/strike]主人公の猿は重装備しているくせに、布の服を着た半分くらいの大きさの蝙蝠と正面からぶつかると、なんと主人公のほうが一方的に吹っ飛ぶ。虚弱体質なのである。
猿であり立派な脚の指をしているくせに、蝙蝠にチョンち小突かれ梁からヌルりと落下していく様を見た時は失笑してしまった。その猿の足指は地面をしっかり掴むためのものではないのか？
「敵の攻撃」と「攻撃の前隙後隙」のバランスも悪かった。特に終盤5章あたりから凄まじく、広範囲の大技に対して後隙は一瞬などということもザラで、なんなら無敵の突進技に繋げてくることすらあり、それに対してこちらは相手に大きなリスクを付けることができないという場面が多発する。つまりこちら側にはジャンケンの「グー」と「チョキ」しかなく、相手は「グー」「チョキ」「パー」を満遍なく連発してくるようなものだ。良くて「あいこ」、ひたすら躱して耐えて一発小突くという、非常に繊細な戦闘をする主人公なのである。

こう書くと良くない印象を与えてしまうかもしれないので明確にしておくが、
個人的にはトータルで見ると余裕のプラスであり、不満を感じながらも夢中になれるくらい楽しいゲーム体験ができた。
しっかりオススメできる。
しかし正直、戦闘バランスに関する低評価レビューの内容にも、「全くその通りだ」と同意してしまう。
少し腰を据えてやらなくてはいけないゲームだ。

Black Myth: Wukong me pareció una auténtica locura de principio a fin. Es uno de esos juegos que te dejan con la sensación de estar viviendo una aventura épica constantemente. Lo que más me impresionó fue lo fiel que se siente a la historia y la mitología de Viaje al Oeste, logrando adaptar ese mundo de una forma espectacular sin perder su propia identidad.

Visualmente es impresionante. Los gráficos están entre los mejores que vi en un videojuego, con escenarios enormes, detalles por todos lados y una dirección artística que hace que cada zona tenga personalidad propia. Muchas veces me encontré frenando simplemente para admirar el paisaje.

Otro de los puntos fuertes es la enorme variedad de enemigos y jefes. Prácticamente siempre aparece algo nuevo que obliga a cambiar la estrategia. Los combates contra los bosses son increíbles, tanto por su diseño como por la espectacularidad de las peleas. Hay enfrentamientos que realmente se sienten memorables y dignos de una gran leyenda.

También me encantó el estilo de juego. El combate es ágil, desafiante y muy satisfactorio. Cada transformación, habilidad y mejora aporta nuevas formas de jugar, haciendo que la experiencia se mantenga fresca durante toda la aventura.

Si tuviera que mencionar algo que no me gustó tanto, sería la sección de la Pagoda y algunas partes de las cárceles. Fueron las únicas zonas que sentí un poco más pesadas o frustrantes en comparación con el resto del juego. Sin embargo, son una pequeña parte dentro de una experiencia que me pareció extraordinaria.

En general, Black Myth: Wukong superó mis expectativas. Su combinación de gráficos impresionantes, adaptación fiel de la mitología, gran variedad de enemigos y jefes, y un sistema de combate excelente lo convierten en uno de los mejores juegos que jugué. Para mí, es una obra espectacular que demuestra lo que puede lograrse cuando se combina pasión, ambición y un diseño de altísimo nivel.

Estoy con muchas ansias de jugar al zhong kui , es una de las pocos estudios de juego que me logro ser uno de sus fanaticos y admirar tanto el trabajo con el unico juego que publicaron.

Black Myth: Wukong - если проходить игру с китайской озвучкой, то игра очень хорошо передаст всю свою атмосферу. Можно будет погрузиться в китайскую мифологию. В этой игры мы будем играть за обезьяну, которой необходимо собрать разбросанные по разным биомам реликвии, чтобы освободить царя обезьян.

Основное оружие - это посох, которым мы всю игру будем лупить обитателей местной флоры и фауны. Когда нам будет этого мало или мы будем не справляться с врагами, то в нашем арсенале имеются различные заклинания, облегчающие сражение с боссами или обычными рядовыми врагами. Заклинаний достаточно много, от заклинаний заставляющих застыть на месте врагов или призвать фантомов для помощи в бою, до заклинаний позволяющих превратиться в ранее поверженного нами босса и уже в его обличие сражаться какое то время с врагом.

Стоит отметить что боевка выглядит задорной и динамичной. Боссов достаточно много, они сделаны хорошо, выглядят классно, анимация атак шикарная. За счет отсутствия штрафа за смерть, возможности перераспределять в любой момент навыки и обширного выбора заклинаний, большой сложности боссы не будут представлять, разве что только в самом начале, пока идет привыкание к боевой системе.

Все локации в игре выглядят прекрасно, очень эффектно сделаны задние планы. Единственное, что портит погружение, это эффект фокусировки, который нельзя отключить, из-за которого в заставках размывается задний фон, акцентируя внимание на переднем плане, что имея такие красивые декорации, портит погружение. Ну и невидимые стены, когда кажется что тут какое то ответвление и впереди будет секрет, а тут всего навсего невидимая стена. Но в целом каждая локация уникальна и не похожа на предыдущую.

Как итог - красивая игра с интересной боевкой, позволяющая погрузиться в китайскую мифологию!

This game absolutely deserved to be Game of the Year in 2024, and I honestly don’t understand how Astro Bot was considered to be a better game. My personal pick would still be Metaphor: ReFantazio, but I can definitely see Black Myth: Wukong being the more popular choice.

The combat is incredibly fun and engaging, and the game never felt particularly difficult to me, so getting through the main story was a breeze. The world is also beautiful and there’s a lot to explore.

My biggest complaints are the amount of missable content and the fact that you’ll probably want to keep a text guide open if you’re going for everything. The narrative can also be difficult to follow if you’re not familiar with Journey to the West, so I’d recommend reading up on the story beforehand. A few achievements also require some RNG-heavy grinding, which I’m not a fan of.

Despite those issues, I had a great time with it. Very good game and absolutely worth playing, especially on sale.

[h1][b]Uma Jornada Épica, mas com Tropeços Técnicos[/b][/h1]

[b]Black Myth: Wukong[/b] é, sem dúvida, um dos títulos mais visualmente impressionantes e ambiciosos dos últimos anos. Baseado no clássico romance chinês [b]"Jornada ao Oeste"[/b], o jogo explora os acontecimentos logo após o término da obra original. Há inúmeras referências ao conto lendário que são citadas ou retratadas ao longo da aventura, desempenhando um papel de extrema importância para a história do game.

Na introdução, você assume o controle do próprio [b]Sun Wukong[/b] — o Grande Sábio "imortal", esbanjando poder e personalidade. Porém, essa experiência dura pouco. O verdadeiro protagonista que você guiará nessa jornada é um macaco genérico (ou melhor, aquele a quem chamam de [b]"O Predestinado"[/b]): um personagem mudo, sem expressões ou personalidade, que aparentemente tem apenas um objetivo: MATAR! 

Brincadeiras à parte, sua missão principal é reunir as relíquias deixadas por Sun Wukong para ressuscitá-lo ou trazê-lo de volta — ao menos segundo o velho macaco da abertura (o que se revela uma enorme mentira no final!).

Com forte inspiração na fórmula Soulslike, o game entrega confrontos memoráveis e um combate extremamente dinâmico. No entanto, a experiência é prejudicada por tropeços no design dos cenários e por problemas de otimização.


[h1][b]Combate e Jogabilidade[/b][/h1]
Black Myth: Wukong foca de forma implacável na esquiva perfeita e no ritmo da ação. A progressão se assemelha muito a um "Boss Rush", intercalado por breves áreas de exploração entre as batalhas principais. Durante os confrontos, a fluidez das esquivas e o peso do impacto dos golpes são extremamente satisfatórios.

O sistema de combate com o bastão brilha através das diferentes posturas (Esmagamento, Pilar e Ofensiva), garantindo uma flexibilidade tática excelente. Aliado a isso, o uso das magias — como paralisar inimigos, criar clones e assumir transformações — adiciona uma camada estratégica essencial que quebra qualquer risco de monotonia.


[h1][b]Direção de Arte e Gráficos[/b][/h1]
Construído na Unreal Engine 5, o jogo é um espetáculo absoluto. Os detalhes nos modelos dos chefes, a iluminação e a densidade dos ambientes são de cair o queixo, e o design das criaturas místicas inspiradas na mitologia chinesa é impecável.

Porém, algo que incomoda bastante é que o título, apesar de lindo, sofre com paredes invisíveis constantes. É muito frustrante tentar explorar um cenário que parece aberto apenas para esbarrar no "ar", o que prejudica demais a imersão e a navegação.


[h1][b]Desempenho e Otimização[/b][/h1]
Infelizmente, a ambição gráfica cobra um preço alto, afetando até mesmo sistemas mais robustos. No meu caso, utilizando um hardware mais antigo (uma GTX 1070), o jogo apresentou alguns problemas de stuttering (engasgos), especialmente durante transições de áreas ou quando muitos efeitos de partículas apareciam na tela simultaneamente.

Apesar disso, a experiência foi perfeitamente jogável e divertida para mim, rodando na qualidade gráfica média e mantendo uma média de 60 FPS em 1440p. Contudo, é inegável que o título exige o uso pesado de tecnologias de upscaling (DLSS/FSR/XeSS) para manter uma taxa de quadros aceitável.


[h1][b]Chefes e Inimigos[/b][/h1]
O grande destaque do jogo fica para as dezenas de chefes — tanto principais quanto opcionais — e para a enorme variedade de inimigos, cada um com mecânicas únicas e fases distintas. A curva de dificuldade é justa, porém exige reflexos rápidos e um bom gerenciamento de mana e estamina.


[h1][b]Platina e os 100%[/b][/h1]
Para quem busca a platina, será necessário terminar o jogo duas vezes (ou quase). No entanto, não é nada muito complicado, já que o New Game Plus (NG+) fica bem mais simples se você tiver feito tudo o que podia na primeira jornada — especialmente o final bom (ou verdadeiro).

O jogo possui dois finais. Optei por não fazer o final ruim (ou falso) porque o verdadeiro é bem mais condizente com a história e com o plano de Sun Wukong. Como mencionei no início desta análise, a narrativa do velho macaco sobre juntar as seis relíquias para ressuscitar Wukong era uma mentira; tudo não passou de um plano do "Grande Sábio" para finalmente se "libertar".

Já para quem quer fazer 100% do jogo (coletando todas as armas, armaduras, itens, etc.), acredito que será necessário jogar cerca de quatro vezes, além de investir algum tempo no farm de recursos.

[hr][/hr]
O jogo vale a pena? Sim, especialmente para fãs de ação rápida e mitologia rica. Embora peque ao nos entregar o controle de um protagonista genérico e sem personalidade, Black Myth: Wukong é um verdadeiro triunfo artístico, com um sistema de combate viciante e chefes memoráveis.

Se a desenvolvedora corrigir os problemas de otimização no futuro e você conseguir relevar o design restritivo de exploração, a jornada do Predestinado é uma experiência que merece ser vivida.

Comprei o jogo em uma promoção e considero o preço justo em relação ao conteúdo oferecido.

[b]Nota final[/b]: 8.5/10

Black Myth Wukong : voici un titre ou quand tu adhères, tu n’arrives plus à t’en décoller. 

L’attente fut longue avant qu’une promo intéressante tombe, mais cela m’a permis de prendre mon mal en patience et de pouvoir savourer le jeu comme on reçoit un cadeau de Noël tant attendu. 
Je savais que j’allais accrocher, ce qui me faisait peur c’est d’invertir de l’argent dans un jeu que potentiellement j’allais arrêter à cause de la difficulté. 

Alors oui, ce jeu est exigeant, il y a du « die and retry » sur quelques boss. Mais, si l’on est bien préparé, que l’on explore bien les recoins, que l’on s’équipe des bons équipements (esprits inclus) et des bons sorts (ceux qui correspondent à notre propre gameplay, il n’y a pas de bon ou mauvais sorts) il est faisable. J’ai déjà bien entamé le chapitre 6, la fin approche petit à petit et déjà je sais que la sensation que ce jeu me procure va me manquer : un investissement personnel dans le LORE et dans la difficulté que peu de jeux savent procurer (suivants les goûts de chacun bien sûr, mais je sais que tout joueur l’a déjà vécu). 

Ma petite conclusion :

Black Myth Wukong est un jeu bien huilé avec une DA de qualité et une histoire racontée telle une suite de fables au fur et à mesure des chapitres. Ce titre tiré de « la pérégrination vers l’Ouest » offre un récit mature dont le joueur saura apprécier son Lore en lisant entre les lignes et en savourant les fins de chapitres. Tous les PNJs sont importants (à dénicher) car ils sont les clés pour la compréhension de l’histoire et apportent ainsi de la profondeur au récit. 

Petite pensée aussi aux arachnophobes (dixit le chapitre 4). Pour information, sur le site Nexus mods, vous pouvez trouver un mod permettant de transformer les araignées en pièces dorées. Si vous voulez jouer sans mod, ce jeu n’est pas pour vous.

After two playthroughs with two different endings, I can honestly say that I’m absolutely satisfied with my purchase. 10/10. I’m still surprised that this game didn’t win Game of the Year in 2024.

Let’s start with the positives.

The world is huge and incredibly detailed. There are massive locations, tons of secrets, and a lot of different quests. There is so much to discover that even just walking around and exploring never gets boring.

The bosses are another big highlight. They all have amazing designs, and overall, I think the difficulty is really well done. Some bosses can definitely give you a hard time, but beating them feels very rewarding. The boss that took me the most attempts was Yellow Loong — around 40 attempts.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3794782417

I also want to give a special mention to what I consider one of the best parts of the entire game: the cinematics after completing each chapter.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3804960394

Oh my god, these are some of the best ways I’ve ever seen a game explain its lore. The art style and animation are absolutely beautiful, and I genuinely couldn’t take my eyes off the screen. Huge respect to the developers for this.

As for the negatives, although I wouldn’t really call this a major flaw compared to everything else the game does so well, the invisible walls can sometimes be annoying. Overall, Black Myth: Wukong is an amazing game, and I 100% recommend buying it. After two playthroughs, I can confidently say that it was absolutely worth it.

What? By Chapter 3 the quality drops insanely off the cliff. Prior chapters were surprisingly fun and came with a promising game total. Not even a hint of the terribleness to come. Sure it wasn’t anything special or masterful even at the beginning chapters but it held my attention greatly. It wasn’t those moments that wanted the player to die and waste time over and over again. Its difficulty felt controlled and managed. Not “insert shameless marketing of ‘prepare to die’ and that being strictly the core design philosophy instead realizing what made the older games great”.

At Chapter 3, you get terrible levels that are just empty and huge with like 4 enemy types that all take the average enemy health pool of Chapter 2 and multiply it by eleven or maybe even more. Of course most of them need only hit you 3 times for you to die while you hit them a thousand. Just picture the weak Undead Hollow of Dark Souls 1 and have it so you have to whale at it 16 times, yeah even those types of enemies get an insane health boost; a complete, blatant waste of time. And you fight probably like a hundred of them by that chapter’s end. Ctr+C and Ctrl+V all throughout, whether by enemies who are made of material much harder than diamonds or the environments which are wide, long and stupidly empty. It’s another sprinting simulator once you reach that chapter (I genuinely don’t get how this became a thing in the 8th gen era of Souls-likes). And the emptiness of those environments are to the absolute uncontrolled, unrestrained maximum lunacy that would make Dark Souls 3 blush (again, I don’t get how this became a thing in the 8th gen era of Souls-likes). It’s a shame, I was really enjoying it up until that awful chapter. Now I truly hope for this genre to die.


+ It barely recovers much from Chapter 4 and onwards. Although it doesn't get anywhere near as bad as Chapter 3, it still has those bad moments sprinkled throughout. Enemies just become more durable. Certain spells become so ridiculously useless like Immobilize or Pluck of Many, with Immobilize just having bosses break through it instantly, as soon as you cast it— doesn't matter if you max them out completely they become useless. All bosses end up feeling the same to point where even the devs started noticing and so some select few of them get "super armor", which just equals to hitting them even more than most; a very consistent philosophy of this game. You're supposed to be an extremely powerful being but it feels no different from the beginning of the game where you're getting on by to the journey of being powerful. It's just higher stat numbers but guess what? Enemies also get higher stat numbers so those stat numbers cancel out the growth. The Souls-like inspirations and direction ruined this game's potential. That genre—trend had no business to be a part of this game. The story as incoherent and what little there was, there was some actual good moments that surprised me, especially around Chapter 4 and onwards. I especially did like the final rowing scene where Bajie (loved this dude) sticks up for his lifelong friend who had left him. English dub was really good. Chapter 3 soured me so much but even then the game has problems. I wish they would just patch that chapter out of the game, honestly. But the Souls-like, "bash your head against the wall for the next hour until finally you beat the boss" will always be a major flaw for it being so unfitting. It should have been a slow, gradual build to a power fantasy experience but it never truly reached that.

Finished it and the combat is what makes this game special. Every fight feels amazing, and the boss designs are some of the best I've ever seen — each one unique in look and playstyle. Animation quality is top notch, and it's not overly hard, so it's more approachable than your typical Soulslike.

Best part of the whole game though? The chapter endings. That painted-art animation with the narrator's voice over it is pure art, genuinely one of the most memorable things in the game.

On the downside, world design is weak — lots of invisible walls and unclear paths that make exploring more frustrating than fun. Story also assumes you already know Journey to the West, so if you haven't read it, you'll miss a lot. No Arabic support either.

Recommended — incredible combat, bosses, and chapter cinematics, held back by messy world design and a story that needs prior knowledge to fully click.

Honestly, I don't even know where to start with this game.

When I first saw Black Myth: Wukong was coming out, it hit me with a kind of nostalgia that I wasn't expecting. I grew up watching Journey to the West on TV when I was a kid. I loved Sun Wukong, I loved the story, and that whole world became something very familiar to me growing up.

So when I saw this game for the first time, I already knew I had to play it.

And because Buddhism has been a part of how I see life, there was something about the themes and stories in this game that connected with me on a deeper level. There were moments where I wasn't just thinking, "This is a cool game." It felt familiar somehow. Like I was seeing a story I grew up with through a completely different lens.

I remember when the game came out. I was still a student and I didn't have a job. My only laptop was an old one with an Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM and a 1TB HDD.

And no graphics card. 💀

I loved story games, but that laptop could barely handle anything. I'd play whatever I could on the lowest settings while watching the game turn into a slideshow whenever things got a little too intense.

Then Black Myth: Wukong came out.

And I remember thinking:

"I don't care. Somehow, I'm going to play this."

Except... I couldn't afford it.

So what did I do?

I watched the entire game on YouTube.

For two days.

I literally watched the whole thing like it was a two-day movie. 😂

It obviously wasn't the same as playing it myself, but at the time, that was the closest I could get. I just wanted to experience the story that badly.

Then last year, things finally started changing for me. I moved abroad, started working while continuing my studies, and eventually managed to buy myself a proper gaming laptop.

I remember checking it on PCGameBenchmark.

My old laptop was something like 10%.

This one?

97%.

I was like:

"YESSSSSSSSS. FINALLYYYYYYYY!!!" 😂

I've never owned a console either. Growing up, I was always the kid sitting next to my friends while they played on theirs. I'd watch them play for hours, and sometimes they'd give me the controller so I could have a turn.

At home, my parents didn't really like me playing games, so I never got a console of my own. Even when I managed to play something, I'd  have to hide it so I wouldn't get caught.

But I had Steam.

And while I was still using that old laptop, I wishlisted Black Myth: Wukong.

With one thought:

"One day, I'm going to play this."

And then, earlier this year, the game went on sale in February.

And my birthday happened to be that same week.

At that point I was like:

"Alright. Say no more. The universe is literally telling me to buy this." 😂

So I bought it on my birthday.

And when I finally launched the game and started playing it myself, I had the exact same excitement I had when I was watching that YouTube gameplay two years earlier.

Except this time, I wasn't watching someone else play.

I was finally playing it.

And now...

I beat it.

There are games you play because they're fun.

There are games you play because they're beautiful.

And then there are games that somehow become connected to your life.

Black Myth: Wukong is one of those games for me.

It's connected to my childhood. To Journey to the West. To sitting beside my friends watching them play games I couldn't own. To playing games on a laptop that could barely run them. To watching this exact game on YouTube because I couldn't afford it. To wishlisting it and telling myself that one day I'd play it.

And then finally getting the chance to.

That's probably why finishing this game feels different.

So to everyone who worked on Black Myth: Wukong — the developers, artists, writers, musicians, voice actors, animators, and everyone else involved:

Thank you.

You didn't just make a game that I enjoyed.

You made something that I had been waiting years to experience.

And I'm definitely not leaving it here. I'm going to start another playthrough because there's still so much I want to see and experience.

But for now...

장점 :

검은 신화 오공은 중국 4대 기서 중 서유기를 모티프로 한 손오공 게임이다. 
작성 기준 무려 3천만 장 이상 판매 게임.
소울 라이크 게임이지만 그렇게 어렵지는 않다. 다만 리듬 게임 같은 엇박 타이밍과 공격 모션의 딜레이 때문에 선 입력에 따른 직관적이지 못한 답답함은 있었다. 다행히 사망 시 패널티 가 없어 마음 편하게 도전하는 재미가 있다.

3가지 봉술 자세를 가지고 바꾸는 재미와 내가 원하는 부분을 선택해서 키워가는 재미가 있다. 물론 초기화도 가능해서 스킬과 장비를 이것저것 조합하는 재미가 상당하다. 능력치를 최대까지 찍으려면 3회차 이상해야 하는데 다양한 조합으로 다회차 도전 재미를 느낄 수 있다. 

아주 아름다운 풍경과 불교의 사찰 등의 배경 그래픽, 장비 그래픽이 굉장히 섬세하고 돋보인다. 자세히 보게 되는 즐거움이 있다.

그리고 또 다른 장점은 매우 다양한 보스와 적 캐릭터가 많다는 점이다. 
일반적인 게임의 경우 색깔 놀이나 돌려 막기 적이 많은데, 이 게임은 특색 있는 많은 적을 만날 수 있고 서유기처럼 여행하던 중 새로운 적을 만나는 느낌이 들어서 더 좋았다. 매번 새로운 적 패턴과 페이즈, 각각 공략하는 재미가 있어 개인적으로 가장 만족한 부분이었다.

게임 하기 전에 서유기를 읽고 나면 더 좋을 것 같다. 

개인적으로 가장 큰 문제점은 투명 벽이라고 생각한다. 갈 수 있는 부분과 갈 수 없는 부분이 너무 애매하고 갈 수 없는 곳을 보이지 않는 벽으로 막아 놓은 맵 구성은 정말 아쉽다.

Black Myth: Wukong jest rewelacyjną grą, choć nie jest wolna od wad. Stawia ona nacisk na ekspresję gracza przez walkę w trakcie epickiej, hermetycznej i enigmatycznej wędrówki głównego bohatera na zachód. Wzorowa prawa audiowizualna zanurza gracza w chińskim folklorze, co dla mnie, jako wschodnioeuropejskiego ignoranta, nie zawsze było czytelne i zrozumiałe, ale w ogóle mi to nie przeszkadzało, będąc tak oczarowanym tą grą. W kwestii błędów, jeśli jest się w stanie zbagatelizować bezczelne niewidzialne ściany, "dziwny" i męczący - a w opinii niektórych tragiczny - level design ( sam do końca nie wiem, jak się czuję z tym, co mi zrobiły niektóre poziomy w Wukongu ), to czeka nas naprawdę wspaniałe doświadczenie. Na pewno pierwszych dwóch rozdziałów. Reszta gry może aż tak nie lśnić, a szczególnie rozdział szósty, który w porównaniu z resztą wydawał się zaskakująco pusty i niedoszlifowany. Może nie było czasu, może zabrakło hajsu, a może to tylko moja opinia. Strukturalnie Wukong przypomina Sekiro, ale z bardziej przyjaznymi graczowi mechanikami. Nie jesteśmy w żaden sposób karani za śmierć, respec słusznej wielkości i pociesznych drzewek umiejętności jest dostępny zawsze i za darmo przy kapliczkach, tak, aby można było sobie okładać kijem multum oryginalnych bossów jak nam się widzi. Mając to wszystko na uwadze, pozytywy i negatywy, wystawiam grze 9,5 na 10 bananów, ale takich dużych i dojrzałych. Reject humanity, embrace the monke.

《黑神话：悟空》给我的感觉，不只是“国产3A终于来了”这么简单，而是真正让我久违地找回了第一次接触大型单机游戏时，那种愿意停下来认真看风景、听对白、研究敌人、反复挑战Boss的感觉。
最让我印象深刻的，是它对中国传统文化的表达。无论是建筑、塑像、妖怪设计，还是音乐、台词和各种细节，都有一种非常熟悉却又充满想象力的味道。它没有简单地把《西游记》重新讲一遍，而是借着我们熟悉的人物和世界观，重新塑造了一个更加苍凉、神秘甚至有些残酷的西游世界。
战斗方面也很有自己的特色。棍法、法术、变身和各种技能组合起来以后，可玩性很高。很多Boss第一次打会觉得压迫感十足，但逐渐摸清招式、调整打法，最后成功击败它们的时候，那种成就感非常强。尤其是一些重要Boss，无论演出、音乐还是招式设计，都属于真正能让人记住的水平。
当然，游戏也不是没有缺点。部分地图的引导比较弱，有些地方容易迷路，空气墙偶尔也会影响探索体验，个别战斗和镜头表现还有提升空间。但这些问题并没有掩盖它整体的完成度。
对我来说，《黑神话：悟空》最难得的地方，是它终于让我看到，中国自己的神话、审美和文化，也完全可以被做成一款具有世界级表现力的大型单机游戏。
它不完美，但足够优秀，也足够特别。
如果你喜欢动作游戏，喜欢西游文化，或者只是想体验一款真正具有中国特色的大型单机作品，我认为它值得一玩。

boss一言不合就是疯狗飞天遁地长连段，其中夹杂大量出手前摇不明显或极具欺骗性（又或是完全没有出手前摇）的快慢刀，变速刀，抽帧刀，这样的设计压根就没给你时间去目押躲避攻击。想象一下有人拿棒球棍打你，棒球棍高高举起晃了晃在一瞬间砸到你脑壳上，棒球棍没有一个由慢到快的加速过程，而是在一瞬间由0加速至非常快的速度。这样的设计贯穿黑猴全流程，最后在杨戬和王灵官等后期boss（包括大圣）集大成。

It's a gorgeous game with cool lore and amazing boss and environment designs, but honestly, it feels like it has a huge identity crisis. It’s trying to be a mix of God of War and a Soulslike, but does both poorly.

You don't get the storytelling or character depth of GoW. The protagonist is silent, and side characters dip in and out so fast you never get a chance to care about them. That hands-off style works fine in something like Elden Ring, but here it just feels hollow. The game basically takes the worst parts of its inspirations.  the maps, while giving the impression of some openness, are super linear, but you're still forced to do really boring exploration just to keep up. Some of the side area and secret stuff is genuinely super good, but you will almost surely miss it if you aren't watching a guide.  If you skip hunting down gear upgrades, the bosses are artificially brutal. But the second you get those upgrades the combat becomes extremely easy, and you can practically stagger lock any boss.

The combat is also in a really weird spot. Basic enemies are complete fodder you can stunlock to death instantly with light attacks, but late-game bosses are the exact opposite. They just dart around (or fly) and relentlessly spam attacks with literally zero openings. I originally wanted to run a Rock Solid/counter-attack build, but it's useless because bosses just attack right through your counters and hit you anyway. Honestly, unless you're using Spear Stance for the i-frames, countering is a trap. I get that learning patterns is the point of a Soulslike, but when they never stop swinging, your only real option is spamming Immobilize just to get a turn. So instead of actual build variety, most fights just devolve into immobilize, mashing light attack 20 times, and dropping a charged heavy.  

Aside from the really good cutscenes at the end of each chapter, the game is just lacking. It misses the narrative pull of God of War and the massive, free exploration of Elden Ring. Between the unbalanced combat and tedious item hunting, it basically just boils down to a very pretty "walk to the next boss" simulator. 

Also, the weapon and armor that is available is a weird selection.  There aren't very many choices, and a lot are locked behind ng+.  I enjoyed using spear stance but the spear stance focused weapon got outscaled later in the game so I just had to stop using it, and it wasn't upgradeable.  The armor I liked was just bad, even when upgraded.  Odd choices,  and it really fit with the theme of the game feeling very railroaded, and like there is only one right way to play.

Do you like unbalanced games that love to waste your time? Are you hankering to watch bosses attack you while you patiently wait your turn for an opportunity? Want to have your quick reflexes rewarded with a giant middle finger? Maybe you want to experience what seems like an interesting story, but you have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clue what's going on. THIS GAME IS FOR YOU!

I'll start with the cons because that's what made this game a mostly miserable experience.

[h2] CONS: [/h2]
[b] Combat [/b]
The horrible feeling of the combat is honestly what ruined this game for me. After coming off of amazing combat in games like Lies of P, Stellar Blade, and Khazan...there's so much to be desired here. You're basically going to be spamming your light attack the entire game and I might be nit picking, but the timing of the light attacks pissed me off the entire game. There is a hint of a "parry", which they call "seeing through", but it's a really ♥♥♥♥ mechanic. Essentially, you have to try and time your attack so that you can try to parry as the enemy attacks you, but the stupidest part? Your parry can just miss entirely and it happens often. Your good timing gets rewarded with nothing. As you progress in the game, enemies start to jump away from you more often, so they can also just jump away from your perfectly timed parry or, even worse, attack you a bunch and then jump away. This game is FULL of long combos from enemies and bosses. I counted 12 attacks from a boss and then when it was my turn to attack, they jumped away and then started their next combo. It's just incredibly ♥♥♥♥ boss design and pacing. And if the boss isn't annoying enough, they give them some status effects, which make the fight even more miserable. Nobody likes to watch the boss do all the cool attacks while you sit and spam dodge. Someone described this game as a dodge simulator and that's perfectly put. Towards the end of your game, your strongest spells and attacks just get negated. The bosses can literally side step your most powerful attack and break out of spells that you've dumped skill points into.

[b] Navigation [/b]
Some of these maps are so confusing and exhausting to trek through that I almost stopped playing, especially in Chapter 3. I'm obsessed with checking every nook and cranny and having no map isn't always a big deal, but so much ♥♥♥♥ looks exactly the same in this game. You don't remember where you've been or where to go next. A path splits into 3 directions. You choose one and it splits into 3 more directions. It's not fun to always be wondering which way is the way the game wants you to go to progress and which way may just have cool side quests or items to discover. And you CAN permanently miss some items if you don't explore enough before moving on. Sometimes you're running in emptiness for WAY too long and your character does NOT move at a fast pace.

[b] Story [/b]
It seemed cool, but I have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clue what was going on. I think if you knew more about Chinese myth it would have been more interesting.

[b] Music [/b]
WHAT MUSIC. You will run around in silence most of the time.

[h2] PROS: [/h2]
Beautiful environments, great English voice acting, very cool character, enemy, and boss models. The first 2 chapters are fun. That's it.

Grand Theft Auto V Legacy — A Thesis on Chaos

> “Man is born free, yet everywhere he is surrounded by loading screens.”



After completing GTA V Enhanced, I decided to return to Legacy.

At first, I thought I was simply playing an older version of the same game.

I was wrong.

I had encountered the Legacy experience.

Enhanced represents technological progress: better lighting, more detailed environments, more demanding graphics. But Legacy asks a deeper question:

Does technological progress necessarily produce a better existence?

I answered:

No.

And suddenly, Schopenhauer made sense.


---

The Ontology of 720p

I play at 720p on Low settings.

Some may see this as a limitation.

I see it as freedom.

1080p asks:

> “Why do you not demand more?”



720p asks:

> “What is enough?”



This is not merely a graphics setting.

It is a philosophical position.


---

The Will to Chaos

Then I discovered Chaos Mod.

Every few moments, reality itself becomes uncertain.

Cars appear where they should not.

NPCs lose their understanding of causality.

Physics becomes a suggestion rather than a law.

At this point, Nietzsche's philosophy becomes unavoidable.

The player must overcome the ordinary boundaries of gameplay and become something greater:

The Über-Gamer.

And then comes the inevitable question:

What if I spawn 30 Boeing 747s on the highway?

Kant cannot answer this.

Hegel would probably call it a dialectic.

Marx would describe it as a class struggle between highway infrastructure and aviation.

Newton would simply resign.


---

The LSPD Problem

Eventually, the Los Santos Police Department arrives.

I run.

They chase me.

Traffic collapses.

The highway becomes an airport.

Thirty 747s exist where cars were supposed to be.

Chaos Mod continues operating.

I begin questioning my own existence.

The planes fall off from the sky.

Yet the game continues.

And here we discover the fundamental truth of Legacy:

> Performance may decline, but the will to chaos persists.




---

Legacy vs Enhanced

Enhanced gave me technological progress.

Legacy gave me freedom.

Enhanced asks:

“How realistic can Los Santos become?”

Legacy asks:

“How many aircraft can the highway philosophically contain?”

I know which question matters more.


---

Final Verdict

GTA V Legacy is not simply an older version of GTA V.

It is a philosophical experiment disguised as an open-world game.

It is about freedom.

It is about limitation.

It is about technology.

It is about chaos.

It is about the eternal human desire to put completely inappropriate vehicles on roads.

Thesis: Modem.
Antithesis: Excavation crew.
Synthesis: No internet.

Final synthesis: GTA V Legacy with 30 Boeing 747s on the highway.

Veni, vidi, Legacy.

Grand Theft Auto V – Timeless Open-World Classic
Despite releasing over a decade ago, GTA V still stands as one of the best open-world games available on Steam in 2026. It perfectly blends a cinematic single-player campaign, a living, interactive open world, and endless multiplayer fun, offering incredible replay value that most modern AAA titles simply cannot match.
Single-Player Experience
The offline story is the game’s greatest strength, featuring a unique three-protagonist system that remains revolutionary to this day. Switching between Michael, Franklin, and Trevor brings constant variety to missions, ranging from thrilling heists and high-speed chases to dark comedic story moments and sharp social satire. The characters are well-written and memorable, with a compelling plot and tons of high-quality side content, easter eggs, and exploration opportunities. The entire campaign is polished, engaging, and well worth the price alone.
Incredibly Immersive Open World
Los Santos and Blaine County create one of the most detailed, alive game maps ever made. With a dynamic day-night cycle, realistic weather, lifelike NPC and traffic behavior, and diverse environments including cities, suburbs, mountains, deserts, and oceans, the world always feels active and authentic. Every corner hides secrets and unique details, making free-roaming exploration endlessly enjoyable. The enhanced PC update adds ray tracing, improved textures, and modern upscaling support, keeping the game visually competitive even today.
GTA Online: Endless Gameplay With Noticeable Flaws
GTA Online is why the game has stayed popular for over ten years. It delivers massive amounts of multiplayer content, including heists, races, stunts, businesses, and full character/vehicle customization. Regular free updates keep the game fresh, offering thousands of hours of fun especially when playing with friends.
However, the online mode has clear downsides. The in-game economy forces heavy repetitive grinding for new players, and Shark Card microtransactions feel predatory and outdated. Public lobbies still suffer from hackers, lag spikes, and occasional crashes. Solo players will find progression slow and tedious, while private lobbies with friends offer a far better experience.
PC Performance & Optimization
The Steam PC version is the definitive way to play GTA V. It features excellent optimization, running smoothly on both low-end and high-end hardware with support for high resolutions and high refresh rates. Load times are greatly improved, and full controller support, customizable settings, and a massive modding community further extend the game’s lifespan infinitely.
Final Verdict
GTA V is a genre-defining classic that ages like fine wine. Its phenomenal single-player, unmatched open-world design, and unlimited replayability easily outweigh its online monetization and hacking flaws. Whether you prefer solo storytelling or chaotic multiplayer fun with friends, it is an essential staple for every Steam library.
Rating: 9/10 — A timeless open-world masterpiece with minor modern drawbacks.

从线下模式开始谈，故事模式才是这游戏吸引我的根本所在，但是，实际体验下来，对于整部剧情我没觉得有多么出彩，但也不至于说不好。而且感觉很多剧情的设计，让我觉得它不是为了讲好故事，而是为了把它的玩法展示出来，让你去体验他的一些玩法设计。而且，三人角色切换的这种设计确实很不错，但从我的体验来讲，它形成了一种割裂，让故事的沉浸感反而变弱了，没办法把自己代入到故事中去。   其次，NPC互动上，如果要求不高的情况下没问题，但是和大表哥2比起来，我觉得差的不是一星半点了。当然毕竟年份在那摆着，有时代局限性很正常。

接下来是线上模式，这也是我最不喜欢的一部分，我不敢说它这个东西好不好，起码对于“独狼、全成就”的我来说，这玩意是一点都不适合我，所以也提醒各位，如果有跟我是同一种类型的玩家，还是别碰它了。首先，单人玩能不能玩？肯定是能的，但是可玩性就没多少了，能单人刷的就那么几个，反反复复的就为了刷点钱，搞资产确实有收益，但是那收益还真就不如刷刷德瑞合约来的快，独狼玩家满仓出货想也别想，送不完。 还有公开战局，疯狗遍地，见人就打，想正常玩游戏那就只能自己开战局，公开送货的加成，别想！    从成就来看，联机成就难不难？难，也不难！如果你有三个固定的搭子（时间充足，不吵架），那这个游戏全成就不难，你们只需要一起玩，一起培养角色，一起磨合就可以了。如果你这个三个固定搭子，恰好是三个大神，那你对来说，全成就可太简单了，毫无难度，一路躺着完成。但如果你跟我一样是，独狼玩家，那你就等着遭罪吧，大多数成就要求4人以上，遍地求人，四处找人带，好话说尽，偶尔碰到素质不好的，作为新人还得忍着挨骂几句，我玩个游戏图的就是开心，怎么感觉越玩越卑微，任务过了，生一肚子气，图什么。最难的成就“罪神”实在忍不了了，刷出来的，当初也是和朋友一起，尝试几次罪神2，打了几天，没过去，心态炸了。其实没多难，多打几次掌握了打法还是挺简单的，但是学习成本太大了吧！！谁也不是24小时打游戏，一天也就能玩个2-3小时，，一旦失败一次，就要从头打，前边的任务就要打上几天，才能又打到上次死的地方。，，这种死亡学习成本，从中体会不到过关的快乐，只有一次次的无奈和想砸键盘。好像一共29个任务吧。每个任务都得20分钟左右，2人过一遍，3人过一遍，4人过一遍，这种安排是实在没啥任务可做了吗？还是故意拖延玩家的游戏时长？

Grand Theft Auto V, conocido como GTA V, es uno de los videojuegos más populares de la saga Grand Theft Auto y uno de los títulos de mundo abierto más reconocidos de los últimos años. Desarrollado por Rockstar Games, el juego combina acción, conducción, exploración y una historia llena de situaciones inesperadas.

Uno de los aspectos que más destaca es su historia, protagonizada por Michael, Franklin y Trevor, tres personajes muy diferentes que terminan trabajando juntos en distintos golpes y negocios ilegales. Cada uno tiene su propia personalidad, problemas y objetivos, lo que hace que la historia sea variada y entretenida. Además, poder cambiar entre los tres personajes durante determinadas partes del juego hace que las misiones sean mucho más dinámicas.

Otro punto fuerte es el mundo abierto. Los jugadores pueden recorrer libremente la ciudad de Los Santos y sus alrededores, utilizando autos, motos, aviones, barcos y otros vehículos. También existen muchas actividades secundarias, como carreras, deportes, compras, exploración y diferentes desafíos, por lo que no es necesario limitarse solamente a las misiones principales.

Los gráficos y la ambientación también son destacables. A pesar de que el juego fue lanzado originalmente en 2013, Rockstar consiguió crear un mundo bastante detallado, con diferentes zonas, personajes y situaciones que hacen que la ciudad parezca estar viva. La banda sonora y las emisoras de radio también aportan mucho a la experiencia.

Por otro lado, GTA V tiene algunos aspectos negativos. Algunas misiones pueden resultar repetitivas después de varias horas y ciertas actividades secundarias no tienen tanta profundidad como otras. Además, el contenido del juego está dirigido a un público adulto debido a su violencia, lenguaje y temáticas.

En conclusión, GTA V es un juego muy completo y entretenido, especialmente para quienes disfrutan de los mundos abiertos y de tener libertad para explorar. Su historia, sus personajes y la gran cantidad de actividades disponibles hacen que siga siendo un juego muy interesante incluso muchos años después de su lanzamiento. Aunque tiene algunos aspectos mejorables, es fácil entender por qué se convirtió en uno de los videojuegos más conocidos y exitosos de la historia

GTA V delivers great gameplay, a huge open world, an okay story, good graphics, great sound design, and a reasonable amount of replayability options.

The gameplay is one of the strongest parts of GTA V. It is the largest GTA game I’ve played, with a massive world and plenty of things to do. There is a decent number of side activities, although some of them can feel surprisingly small compared to the size of the world. I also like that you can play as three different characters, with Michael, Franklin, and Trevor each having their own unique abilities and playstyles. The shooting is better than San Andreas, although I personally prefer the shooting in GTA IV. Driving motorcycles is also much better than in GTA IV, while the game allows you to fly much larger planes. There are lots of different weapons to use, and the game has some amazing missions, although there are also a few boring ones. One thing I wish GTA V allowed was entering more restaurants and other buildings.

The story is okay. Having three protagonists makes the story more interesting, and there are plenty of memorable moments throughout the campaign. However, I found some parts less interesting than other GTA games, and the story doesn't reach the same level for me as GTA IV.

The graphics are good, especially considering the size of the open world. Los Santos and Blaine County have plenty of detail, and the game still looks pretty good today, although the visuals are becoming somewhat outdated.

The sound design is great. The weapon sounds, vehicles, environmental audio, character dialogue, and radio stations all help make the world feel alive. The soundtrack is also enjoyable, even if I don't find it as memorable as some previous GTA games.

For replayability, GTA V has a reasonable amount of options. There are side activities, collectibles, different missions, character switching, and GTA Online. However, some of the activities feel smaller than I expected from such a massive game, which limits how much I want to return to the game.

Overall, GTA V is a great game with great gameplay, an okay story, good graphics, great sound design, and a reasonable amount of replayability. It has some excellent missions and a massive world to explore, but certain activities feel small, some missions are boring, and I prefer GTA IV's shooting and story.

队友手欠开枪惊扰了女巫，原本安静啜泣的女鬼瞬间扑过来秒人；有人乱跑落单，被 smoker 拖进角落，全队慌忙冲过去救人；好不容易打到安全屋门口，身后尸潮和坦克追着屁股撵，一边嘶吼一边挤进门，最怕损友顺手把门关上把你锁在外边等死。
全程充斥着此起彼伏的 “救我！”“身后有 hunter！”“别乱开枪啊！”，就算频繁翻车通关失败，四个人笑得停不下来，压力瞬间全释放，解压效果一绝。
游戏里的 AI 导演是它的灵魂，也是百玩不腻的关键。系统会盯着我们全队血量、弹药存量、走到哪段路，随时调整僵尸数量、特感刷新位置。哪怕反复刷同一张官方地图，每一局遭遇全都不一样：有时候一路顺风顺水尸潮很少，有时候刚出门就被连刷好几个特殊感染者围殴，永远猜不到下一秒会发生什么，完全不会打几遍就腻。
近战武器绝对是二代对比一代最大的惊喜。斧头、砍刀、武士刀、电锯，甚至平底锅、棒球棒全都能用。狭窄楼道被僵尸围住时，挥刀劈砍的打击感超舒服，拿平底锅挨个敲僵尸脑袋，搞笑又解压，是我休闲局最爱玩的玩法。
几种特殊感染者设计放到现在依旧堪称教科书：跳脸扑人的猎人、拖人舌头烟鬼、冲撞壮汉、自爆胆汁胖子、一碰就秒杀的女巫、终极 boss 坦克，每种怪应对方式完全不同。慢慢摸索出配合技巧之后，通关成就感特别足。
能坚挺十几年不倒，最大功臣：创意工坊海量 MOD 自由改造
原版本体内容其实不算多，5 个官方战役打完新鲜感就会下滑，但创意工坊直接把游戏可玩性拉到无限大，也是我一直舍不得弃坑的核心原因：
角色替换：原版四个人玩腻了，随便打个 MOD 就能换成原神、星穹铁道、动漫、影视人物，自己组建专属小队；
武器全覆盖：现代枪械、科幻光剑、二次元模型应有尽有，想玩什么枪都能装；
上万张自制地图：国风小镇、恐怖解谜地图、其他游戏移植关卡、欢乐整活图，内容量远超官方几十倍；
玩法随心改：无限子弹、丧尸变种、休闲爽玩难度、硬核炼狱模式，自己就能搭建专属规则。
我平时没事就翻翻工坊装新模组，每次打开游戏都有全新体验，永远不会玩到头。
门槛极低，任何人都能上手
配置要求友好到离谱，十几年前的老旧笔记本、办公电脑都能流畅跑 60 帧，低配党福音。
价格更是性价比天花板，Steam 常年打折史低只要 4 块钱，一瓶矿泉水的价钱，换来上千小时联机时光，找不到第二款这么划算的合作游戏。
没空约朋友的时候，单人开黑也没问题，AI 队友很靠谱，会主动给你药、拉倒地的你、帮忙清理僵尸，独自慢慢闯关也不会枯燥。
实话实说缺点，不盲目吹
原生画质年代太久远
毕竟是 2009 年的老游戏，原版建模、光影粗糙，画面放到现在完全比不上新 3A 大作。好在打高清材质、光影 MOD 之后，画面质感能提升一大截，可以完美弥补这个短板。
对抗 PVP 模式环境很差，千万别随便碰路人房
8 人对战，4 人人类 4 人操控特感伏击的模式，创意挺好，但公共服务器开挂、骂人、新手犯错就被踢的人特别多，戾气很重。想玩 PVP 只建议和熟人自建房间游玩TapTap。
V 社早就停止官方更新了
这么多年没有新战役、新怪物、新角色推出，所有新鲜内容全都依靠玩家自制模组，不喜欢折腾 MOD 的话，本体很快就会玩腻。
新手打专家难度极易受挫
简单、普通难度随便玩玩很轻松，但高级、专家难度容错率极低，僵尸伤害巨高，乱走一步就全队团灭，纯新手直接挑战高难度很容易心态炸裂。
到底谁适合买，谁没必要入手
✅ 强烈推荐：
经常和室友、好友想找联机游戏打发闲暇时间；
喜欢丧尸题材、射击生存，偏爱轻松欢乐的合作氛围；
电脑配置一般，想找不吃性能的耐玩大作；
喜欢折腾模组、自定义游戏内容；
怀旧经典 FPS，看重扎实舒服的射击手感。
❌ 不太适合：
极致画面党，只追求顶级画质、3A 视觉体验；
基本独自游玩，完全不需要联机社交；
胆子很小，受不了突然惊吓、惊悚氛围。
最后总结
求生之路 2 从来不是画面顶尖、玩法复杂的大作，但它把四人合作开黑的乐趣、末日生存的紧张感、自由改造的可玩性做到了极致。这么多年陆续出了无数丧尸合作游戏，却始终没能替代它的位置。
只要你有能凑在一起打游戏的朋友，四块钱买下它绝对稳赚不亏，一局局并肩逃生、互相整活的回忆，远比通关本身更珍贵。

Left 4 Dead 2 is a game about teamwork, survival, and discovering exactly how quickly four people can completely abandon the concept of teamwork.

The premise is simple.

You're trapped in the middle of a zombie apocalypse.

There are thousands of infected.

You have guns.

Your objective is to get from point A to point B without becoming zombie food.

Easy.

Until you play with friends.

The game starts off fairly calm. You grab a weapon, pick up some supplies, and start walking through whatever horrible place the survivors have been thrown into this time.

Then someone shoots a car.

Everyone looks at them.

“Why did you shoot the car?”

“I didn't know it would make noise.”

The alarm starts.

Hundreds of zombies appear.

Everyone starts screaming.

Welcome to Left 4 Dead 2.

The special infected are what make the game so much fun. Regular zombies are bad enough, but then you hear a noise and realize something much worse is coming.

Smoker?

Someone's getting dragged away.

Hunter?

Someone's getting tackled.

Boomer?

Congratulations, you're covered in vomit.

Charger?

There goes your teammate.

Jockey?

Someone is being ridden into a wall.

Tank?

RUN.

The Tank is the game's way of asking whether your team has actually been paying attention.

Usually, the answer is no.

You hear the music.

Everyone freezes.

“Tank.”

Someone says it quietly.

You all immediately start running in different directions.

One person gets separated.

Someone falls off a ledge.

Another person forgets to heal.

The Tank punches someone through a wall.

Now you're down a player.

Great teamwork.

The campaign design is also fantastic. Every level feels like a journey rather than just a collection of rooms, and you're constantly moving toward some kind of safe room while trying to survive whatever the Director decides to throw at you.

And that's one of the best parts of the game.

The game seems to know exactly when you're getting comfortable.

You haven't seen anything dangerous for a while.

Your health is good.

You have plenty of ammunition.

You start thinking:

“This is going pretty well.”

Then the Director decides that you're having too much fun.

A horde appears.

A Witch is nearby.

A Tank spawns.

The lights go out.

Someone screams.

Your entire team collapses.

You make it to the safe room with 12 HP and absolutely no supplies.

Perfect.

The AI Director keeps every game feeling slightly different, which is a huge reason L4D2 has remained so replayable.

You can play the same campaign multiple times and still have completely different experiences.

Maybe you get an easy run.

Maybe you get attacked by three special infected simultaneously.

Maybe your friend gets dragged into a hole and you have to rescue them.

Maybe someone accidentally triggers the alarm and turns the entire level into a zombie festival.

You never really know.

And then there's versus mode.

This is where friendships go to die.

Playing as the survivors is one thing.

Playing as the infected is something completely different.

You get to become the exact creatures that have been ruining everyone's day.

You hide around a corner.

You wait.

You see a survivor walk past.

You spawn.

You attack.

You get killed immediately.

You respawn.

You try again.

Eventually you manage to pull someone off a roof as a Smoker and feel like a tactical genius.

Then a shotgun deletes you.

Back to the respawn screen.

The game is also ridiculously fun with friends because the chaos creates stories you'll remember long after the match ends.

You don't remember every normal round.

You remember the time your friend got launched off a bridge.

You remember someone accidentally shooting the Witch.

You remember hiding in a closet while a Tank destroyed everything outside.

You remember the guy who refused to heal because he was “saving the medkit.”

You remember him dying thirty seconds later.

And somehow, despite all the chaos, the game still rewards actual teamwork.

Stick together.

Share supplies.

Cover each other.

Revive your teammates.

Watch for special infected.

Don't wander off.

It's incredibly simple advice.

Nobody follows it.

Someone always runs ahead.

Someone always gets grabbed.

Someone always says, “I got this.”

They do not have this.

Left 4 Dead 2 is one of those games that feels timeless because it doesn't need complicated progression systems or endless grinding to stay fun.

You pick a campaign.

You grab a gun.

You shoot zombies.

You survive.

You die.

You laugh.

You restart.

And somehow you're still playing hours later.

It's chaotic, funny, tense, and one of the best examples of co-op gaming at its absolute best.

10/10.

I've survived the zombie apocalypse countless times, but I've never survived playing with my friends.

Uno de esos juegos que siguen siendo divertidos incluso muchos años después de su lanzamiento. Su combinación de acción, cooperación y zombis hace que jugarlo con amigos sea especialmente entretenido. Aunque también se puede jugar offline, recomendaría encarecidamente jugarlo con amigos ya que es una experiencia inolvidable.

El juego no solo trae nueva campaña sino que también trae la de la entrega anterior por lo que en esencia estas comprando un 2x1. Además, sus distintos modos de juego como el versus o la gasolina son super divertidos, sobre todo cuando juegas como zombie. Destaco el modo contrarreloj y oleadas, los cuales ofrecen retos de mayor dificultad para los más experimentados.

Uno de sus mayores puntos fuertes es la gran cantidad de contenido disponible gracias a la comunidad. El juego permite añadir mods, texturas, personajes, armas, sonidos y mapas creados por otros jugadores, lo que amplía muchísimo la experiencia. Gracias a esto, es posible encontrar campañas completamente nuevas y modificaciones que cambian la forma de jugar, haciendo que el juego tenga una enorme rejugabilidad.

Lo peor del juego a mi punto de vista es que se le notan los años, las texturas se ven anticuadas, los diseños de personajes son pobres y se vuelve repetitivo a las pocas misiones. Por eso mismo recomiendo meterle mods para que no se haga tan pesado, ya que la campaña aunque no lo parezca es bastante extensa. 

Mi nota final es un 7,5/10. Quitando los mods y demás añadidos del workshop el juego base es un muy buen juego, ojala los de Valve hagan una secuela o remake de esta saga porque se lo merece.

Left 4 Dead 2 parece a simple vista un juego sobre matar infectados y llegar al siguiente refugio, pero después de jugarlo uno puede darse cuenta de que quizás nunca se trató realmente de eso. El mundo ya terminó, no existen grandes héroes ni una promesa de que todo volverá a ser como antes, solo quedan cuatro personas caminando entre ciudades vacías, carreteras destruidas y lugares que alguna vez estuvieron llenos de vida, y aun así siguen avanzando. Cada partida comienza de la misma manera: correr, disparar, ayudar al que quedó atrás y buscar un lugar seguro, pero siempre hay algo que se repite; alguien cae, alguien vuelve por él y, aunque a veces sobrevivimos y otras veces no, siempre queda esa necesidad de continuar. Quizás eso sea lo que hace especial a Left 4 Dead 2: en un mundo donde aparentemente ya no queda nada por salvar, los personajes todavía eligen salvarse entre ellos. No importa cuántos infectados aparezcan ni cuánto caos haya alrededor, cuando un compañero queda atrás todo lo demás deja de importar, porque sobrevivir no significa simplemente llegar al final, sino no dejar de caminar incluso cuando no sabés qué hay al otro lado. Tal vez por eso, cuando termina una campaña, queda una sensación extraña: no ganaste una guerra ni arreglaste el mundo, simplemente llegaste un poco más lejos que antes, pero cuando todo se derrumba, quizás eso sea suficiente.

Left 4 Dead 2 - одна из тех игр, к которым можно возвращаться спустя годы, и она всё ещё нормально играется.

В первую очередь нравится сам геймплей: стрельба ощущается приятно, оружия достаточно, заражённые разнообразные, а особые заражённые заставляют постоянно следить за ситуацией. Благодаря Director'у прохождения не ощущаются полностью одинаковыми - игра умеет подкинуть проблем именно тогда, когда их совсем не ждёшь.

Кампаний много, и каждая по-своему запоминается. При этом кроме обычного прохождения есть Versus, Survival, Mutations и другие режимы, так что после нескольких кампаний игра не заканчивается.

Отдельный плюс - огромное количество пользовательских модификаций и карт. Даже спустя столько лет в игре всё ещё есть чем заняться.

Да, игра уже далеко не новая, но это тот случай, когда возраст практически не мешает. Геймплей до сих пор работает отлично, а кооператив с друзьями вообще остаётся одним из главных достоинств игры.

Хороший кооперативный шутер, который вполне заслуживает того, чтобы его периодически запускать снова.

L4D2 was released in 2009 and is still bringing people together 17 years later. That’s a pretty remarkable accomplishment.
I’m sure a lot of people would agree: It’s 2026, so make L4D3!
I know I wouldn’t be the only person to buy it in a heartbeat.

I have loved this game for YEARS; well over a decade, at this point. I've only recently picked it back up to play again, and it has aged incredibly well. Its simple, frenetic gameplay is perfect for a close group of friends to have an easygoing time, OR for people looking for a more intense and nuanced PvP experience. There are a ton of mods available, if desired, including locations such as Helm's Deep from Lord of the Rings, and even the Titanic. It may not be perfect, but there is a good reason why game companies have been trying to replicate the formula repeatedly over the years. As far as I'm concerned, there has yet to be a better pick-up-and-play multiplayer game than this.
